items.slavonic_text: Чꙋ́жде є҆́стъ беззако́нникомъ бл҃гозако́нїе, и҆ стра́нно невѣ́рнымъ Бг҃оразꙋ́мїе. І҆ꙋде́е же сїѐ ѿри́нꙋша за беззако́нїе, тѣ́мже и҆ є҆ди́ни са́ми на сѧ доба́виша, ꙗ҆́коже Смоко́вница, кля́твꙋ:.
items.english_text: *Ode 9. Heirmos:* *Heirmos: Unto Him Who was manifested on the mountain...* Virginity is alien unto mothers, and childbearing is strange unto virgins: yet in thee, O Theotokos, both were accomplished. Therefore all the generations of the earth unceasingly magnify thee![^166]

items.slavonic_text: Взалка̀ чл҃ческаго сп҃сенїя, хлѣ́бъ сы́и жи́зни Хс҃ и҆ Бг҃ъ мо́й. тѣ́мже смоко́вницꙋ пре́варнаго, безпло́дное Събо́рище, ли́ствїемъ ѡ҆брастꙋ́ши зако́ннымъ, ꙗ҆́коже оу҆зрѣ̀, прокля́тъ:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 1:* Chastity is alien unto the ungodly, and transgression of the Law is strange unto the righteous. But great Joseph turned away from sin and embraced chastity, truly an icon and likeness of Christ!

items.slavonic_text: Же́злъ оу҆́бѡ Мѡѷсе́овъ дре́вле въ Змї́и, А҆аро́новъ же же́злъ въ зелено преложи́ся, и҆ процвѣ́те листїе: непло́дное же и҆со́хшее събо́рище законопрестꙋ́пное, внепло́днꙋю преложи́ся смоко́вницꙋ.
items.english_text: *Troparion 2:* Good order is alien unto lawless ones, and the knowledge of God is strange unto the faithless. But the Jews rejected this through lawlessness: therefore they alone brought upon themselves a curse, like the fig tree!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Гото́ви І҆ꙋде́а І҆ере́я твоя̀, оу҆стро́й рꙋ́цѣ къ Бг҃ооу҆би́йствꙋ. Се́ бо прїи́де кро́ткїй и҆ молчали́выи на стрⷵть, а҆́гнецъ сыи и҆ па́стырь нашъ Хс҃ Цр҃ь Їил҃евъ:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 3:* Hungering for the salvation of mankind, Christ my God, Who is the Bread of Life: when He beheld the fig tree of the deceitful one—the barren assembly overgrown with legalistic leaves—He cursed it![^167]

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Прїимѝ І҆оуде́а, Цр҃я: се́ бо на стрⷵть прихо́дитъ во́лею, да постра́ждетъ и҆ сп҃сетъ зовꙋ́щыѧ непреста́ннѡ, бл҃венъ грѧды́й сп҃ти Крⷵто́мъ вся́ческая.
items.english_text: *Troparion 4:* The rod of Moses of old was changed into a serpent, and the rod of Aaron turned into greenery and blossomed with leaves;[^168] but the barren and withered assembly of transgressors was transformed into a barren fig tree!

items.english_text: *Troparion 8:* Thou didst curse the barrenness of the Law, as leaves burgeoning with the letter of knowledge but bearing no fruit of good works because of lawlessness: but make us all sons of grace of Thy good pleasure![^172]

items.slavonic_text: И҆ ны́нѣ: Приво́димъ ти въ мл҃твꙋ Бц҃ꙋ: тоя̀ мл҃твами и҆ А҆пⷵтолъ твои́хъ, ѡ҆бє́щники ны сътворѝ Бл҃го бл҃гихъ твои́хъ, и҆ свѣ́тлости сподо́би сп҃се Въскр҃сенїя твоегѡ́:.
items.english_text: It is alien unto lawless ones to glorify Thee, the unoriginate Essence, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, the uncreated Almighty Dominion, by Which the whole world was made through the nod of Thy divine power!

provenance.verbatim_source: It is alien unto lawless ones to glorify Thee, the unoriginate Essence, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, the uncreated Almighty Dominion, by Which the whole world was made through the nod of Thy divine power!

items.slavonic_text: ВЪ СТ҃ЫИ И҆ ВЕЛИ́КЇИ ПН҃ЛНИКЪ НА ОУ҆́ТРНИ. Гле́тъ Їере́и: Бл҃венъ Бг҃ъ на́. И҆ мы̀: А҆минь. Трⷵто́е, и҆ Покло́нѡвъ, г҃. По Ѻ҆́тче на́шъ. Гдⷭ҇и поми́лꙋй, в҃і. Прїидѣ́те поклони́мся, г҃. Та́же, Шестоѱа́лмы. и҆ Е҆ктенѝ. Посемъ, А҆ллилꙋ́їа, на Гласъ, и҆́. Великогла́снѡ, и҆ сладкопѣ́ннѡ. Сті́, а҆. Ѿ но́щи оу҆́треннюетъ дꙋ́хъ мои к тебѣ̀ Бж҃е. сті́, в҃. Пра́вдѣ навꙋчи́теся живꙋ́щїи на землѝ. сті́, г҃. Приложи и҆́мъ зла Гдⷭ҇и приложи: сті́, д҃. Та́кѡ бы́хомъ възлюбленному.
items.english_text: We bring unto Thee the Theotokos in intercession: through her prayers and those of Thine Apostles, make us partakers of Thy good things, O Good One, and vouchsafe us the radiance of Thy Resurrection, O Savior!

items.slavonic_text: Пое́мъ Чте́нїя, в Толко́ва: Є҆ѵл҃їа, є҆́же ѿ Мат: Сло́во ѡ҆ Дни І҆ѡа́нна Златооу҆́стагѡ. Ѡ҆ И҆ссо́хшой смоко́вници, є҆мꙋ́же Нача́ло: И҆́кѡже оу҆́бѡ ви́дя. и҆ли двѣ̀: И҆ сло́во Дамаски: ѡ҆ И҆ссо́хший смоко́вници. И҆ ѡ҆ При́тчи Виногра́да. Подо́вже на навѣ́нїе и҆ бесѣ́дꙋ. Ѡ҆бы́чным же ѡ҆ставля́ютсѧ. Посемъ, ѱало́мъ, н҃. Та́же Сп҃си Бг҃ъ лю́ди своя: Гдⷭ҇и поми́лꙋй, в҃і.
items.english_text: Behold, the Bridegroom comes at midnight, and blessed is the servant whom He shall find watching; but unworthy again is the servant whom He shall find careless. Beware therefore, O my soul, lest thou be weighed down with sleep, lest thou be given over unto death, and be shut out from the Kingdom; but awake, crying aloud: Holy, holy, holy art Thou, O God: through the Theotokos, have mercy on us![^174] *(Chanted 3 times with a loud voice.)*

provenance.verbatim_source: Behold, the Bridegroom comes at midnight, and blessed is the servant whom He shall find watching; but unworthy again is the servant whom He shall find careless. items.english_text: The present day brings brightly the beginnings of the Lord's Passions. Come therefore, ye lovers of the feast, let us meet Him with hymns! For the Creator comes to accept the Cross, interrogations and scourging, judged by Pilate: therefore, struck on the head by a servant, He endures all things to save man. Therefore let us cry aloud unto Him: O Lover of mankind, Christ God, grant remission of sins unto those who worship Thy most pure Passions in faith!

[Нд҃лѧ бо дн҃ь Пе́рвыи гле́тсѧ оу҆ Е҆́ллины и҆ Латі́нѡ.] И҆рмо́съ, пов. Тропа́: на в҃і. Послѣди И҆рмо́съ ѡ҆́ба ли́ка вкꙋ́пѣ. Гла́съ, в҃. Пѣ́нь, а҃. И҆рмо́. items.slavonic_text: Въ ст҃ы́й и҆ вели́кїи Пн҃лникъ, па́мять тво́римъ Бл҃же́ннаго І҆ѡ́сифа прекра́снагѡ, и҆ и҆ссо́хшїя смоко́вници: зане́же нача́ло ѿсю́дꙋ прїе́млютъ ст҃ыя стрⷵти Гдⷭ҇а на́шегѡ І҆с҃а Хрⷭ҇та̀. items.english_text: On Holy and Great Monday, we commemorate the blessed Joseph the All-Comely, and the withered fig tree: because from this point the holy Passions of our Lord Jesus Christ take their beginning, and Joseph is first received as a type of Him. For he was the younger son of the Patriarch Jacob, born unto him of Rachel; and he was envied by his brothers on account of certain dreams. First hidden in the digging of a pit; and his father, deceived by the children with the blood-stained garment, grieved, thinking that he had been devoured by a beast. Then he was sold for thirty pieces of silver unto the Ishmaelites, who in turn sold him unto Potiphar, the chief of the eunuchs of Pharaoh, King of Egypt. And when his mistress raged against the chastity of the youth—because he refused to commit iniquity—he left his garment and fled; and she slandered him unto his master, and bonds and a bitter prison received him. Then, on account of the interpretation of dreams, he was brought forth, and shown unto the King, and appointed lord of all the land of Egypt. And again, on account of the distribution of grain, he was revealed unto his brethren. And having well spent the whole course of his life, he died in Egypt, renowned for his great chastity alongside his other virtues. This is a type of Christ: for Christ also was envied by His fellow Jews, and sold by His Disciple for thirty pieces of silver, and shut up in the dark and gloomy pit of the Tomb; and bursting forth thence by His own sovereign power, He reigns over Egypt—that is, over every sin—and utterly overcomes its dominion. And He rules over all the world, and in His love for mankind redeems us, the mystical Giver of grain, since He gave Himself for us, and nourishes us with heavenly Bread, His own Life-bearing Flesh. For this reason, then, the all-comely Joseph is commemorated today.[^185]

items.slavonic_text: въ никопа́нїе ро́ва съкрыва́емъ быва́етъ. и҆ Ѻ҆ц҃ъ є҆го̀, ѡ҆ дѣ́тей преле́стїю ѡ҆кровавле́нїа дѣ́ля ри́зы оу҆страда́етсѧ. ꙗ҆́кѡ ѿ звѣ́ри и҆з̾я́денъ бы́стъ. та́же на три́десятехъ Сре́бреницѣхъ прода́нъ быва́етъ І҆смаили́тѡмъ, и҆́же па́ки преподава́ютъ є҆го̀ Пентефрі́ю нача́лникꙋ скопце́мъ Царя̀ Е҆гѵ́петскагѡ Фараѡ́на. Неи҆сто́вствовавшей же Госпожѝ є҆го̀ на цѣломꙋ́дрїе Ю҆́ноши, поне́же беззако́нїа съдѣ́лати не въсхотѣ̀, ри́зꙋ ѡ҆ста́вль ѡ҆бѣжа̀: сїя́ же Господи́нꙋ є҆го̀ ѡ҆блега́етъ, и҆ въ оу҆́зы и҆ те́мница го́рькая сего̀ прїе́млетъ. Та́же разрѣше́нїя ра́ди снѡ́въ и҆зводи́тся, и҆ Царю̀ явля́емъ быва́етъ, и҆ Гдⷭ҇инъ всея̀ земля̀ Е҆гѵ́петскїя поставлѧ́етсѧ. Па́ки же пшеницода́телства ра́ди Бра́тїи ꙗ҆вленъ быва́етъ. И҆ вся́ческое своегѡ̀ живота̀ до́брѣ препроводи́въ, въ Е҆гѵ́птѣ оу҆мира́етъ, вели́кїй ѡ҆ цѣломꙋ́дрїи при и҆́нѣхъ є҆гѡ̀ до́брыхъ познава́емый. Ѡ҆́бразъ же се́й Хв҃ъ: зане́ и҆ Хс҃ ѿ є҆диноплеме́нныхъ І҆оуде́и зави́ствованъ быва́етъ, и҆ ѿ Оу҆чени́ка на три́десятехъ Сре́бреницѣхъ продае́тся, и҆ въ мра́чный и҆ те́мный ро́въ Гро́бъ заключа́ется, и҆ ѿтꙋ́дꙋ самовла́стнѡ въсто́ргнꙋвся Црⷵтвꙋетъ на Е҆гѵ́птомъ, та́же и҆ на грѣсѣ̀ вся́цѣмъ, и҆ по держа́вѣ сего̀ побѣжда́етъ: мі́ромъ же всѣ́мъ ѡ҆блада́етъ, и҆ чл҃колю́бнѡ и҆скꙋпꙋ́етъ ны, та́инственныи пшеницода́телъ ꙗ҆́кѡ са́мъ себѐ заны̀ давы́й, и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ пита́етъ насъ нбⷭ҇нымъ Хлѣ́бомъ, свое́ю Живоно́сною Пло́тїю. Посемꙋ̀ оу҆́бѡ Сложе́нїю Прекра́сный І҆ѡ́сифъ нн҃ѣ прїе́млется. Зде́ же и҆ ѡ҆ И҆ссо́хшей смоко́вници Па́мять творимъ: зане́же Бж҃твеннїи Е҆ѵл҃істы, Си́рѣчь, Матѳе́й и҆ Ма́рко, по Повѣ́сти ѡ҆ Ва́їяхъ прино́сѧтъ: въ оу҆́трїе же и҆зше́дши и҆мъ ѿ Виѳані́а, взалка̀. Дрꙋгі́й же, Оу҆́трѣ же возвра́щся въ Гра́дъ, гле́тъ, взалка̀, и҆ ви́дѣвъ смоко́вницꙋ ли́ствїе то́кмѡ и҆мꙋ́щꙋю. не бѣ́ бо вре́мя смо́квамъ: прїи́де къ не́й, и҆ е҆гда̀ пло́да не ѡ҆брѣ́те на не́й, речѐ, да не ктомꙋ̀ пло́дъ ѿ тебѐ бꙋ́детъ въ вѣ́къ: И҆ а҆́бїе и҆́сше смоко́вница. Смоко́вница оу҆́бѡ є҆́стъ: Со́нмище І҆оуде́йское, на не́мже пло́да подо́бнаго Сп҃съ не ѡ҆брѣ́тъ, то́чїю ѡ҆сѣня́ющее зако́на, и҆ сїѐ ѿя́тъ ѿ ни́хъ, пра́здно вся́чески съдѣ́лавъ. А҆́ще ли же кто̀ рече́тъ, почто̀ бездꙋ́шное дре́во сꙋ́хо бы́сть кля́твꙋ взе́мше не согрѣши́вшее; Да навы́кнетъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ І҆оуде́и зрѧ́ще Хрⷭ҇та при́снѡ всѣ́хъ бл҃годѣ́телствꙋюща, никомо́же кля́тичноє и҆ско́рно содѣ́лавша, непщева́хꙋ ꙗ҆́кѡ си́лꙋ и҆́матъ то́чїю бл҃годѣ́телствовати, злотвори́ти же, ни. Чл҃колюбе́цъ же Влⷣка Сн҃ъ, не въсхотѣ̀ на чл҃вцѣ се показа́ти, и҆ семꙋ̀ бы́ти, да оу҆́бѡ оу҆вѣ́рятъ неблагода́рныѧ лю́ди, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆́матъ си́лꙋ и҆ къ мꙋ́цѣ дово́лнꙋю, ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ же не хо́щетъ, на бездꙋ́шномъ и҆ нечꙋ́вственномъ є҆стествѣ̀ мꙋче́нїе съдѣва́етъ. Вкꙋ́пѣ же нѣ́кое и҆ неизглаго́ланное Сло́во є҆́стъ, ѡ҆ ста́рецъ Премꙋ́дрыхъ к намъ пресяжде́нное. items.english_text: On this day also we commemorate the withered fig tree: because the divine Evangelists, namely Matthew and Mark, record after the account of the Palms: on the morrow, as they went out from Bethany, He hungered. And the other says: returning in the morning into the city, He hungered; and seeing a fig tree having leaves only—for it was not the season of figs—He came to it, and when He found no fruit upon it, He said: Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward unto the age! And immediately the fig tree withered away.[^186] Now the fig tree signifies the Jewish synagogue, upon which the Savior found not the fitting fruit, but only the shadow of the Law; and this He took away from them, leaving it entirely destitute. And if anyone should say: Why did the soulless tree, which had not sinned, become dry after receiving a curse? Let him learn that the Jews, seeing Christ always doing good unto all, and having never brought anything painful or grievous upon anyone, supposed that He had power only to do good, but not to work harm. But the Master and Son, the Lover of mankind, would not show this upon a man, that the ungrateful people might indeed be convinced that He possesses sufficient power unto punishment also; yet since as God He desires not to punish man, He worked this chastisement upon a soulless and insensible nature. Together with this, there is also a certain ineffable teaching handed down to us from the ancient wise elders, as Saint Isidore of Pelusium says: that this was the tree of transgression, whose leaves the transgressors needed for a covering; therefore it was cursed by Christ in His love for mankind, since it had not suffered this then, that it might no longer bear fruit that was the cause of sin. And that sin is likened unto a fig is manifest: for it possesses the sweetness of sensual pleasure, the stickiness of guilt, and afterwards the hardening and prickling of the conscience. Nevertheless, by the Fathers, the narrative of the fig tree is placed here for the sake of compunction, just as that of Joseph is placed here because he bears the type of Christ. For the fig tree is every soul destitute of all spiritual fruit; wherein in the morning, after this present life, the Lord finding no rest in her, withers her with a curse and sends her into the eternal fire. And she stands as a withered pillar, striking fear into those who do not bring forth the fitting fruit of virtues. Through the prayers of the all-comely Joseph, O Christ our God, have mercy on us, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^187]

provenance.verbatim_source: On this day also we commemorate the withered fig tree: because the divine Evangelists, namely Matthew and Mark, record after the account of the Palms: on the morrow, as they went out from Bethany, He hungered. And the other says: returning in the morning into the city, He hungered; and seeing a fig tree having leaves only—for it was not the season of figs—He came to it, and when He found no fruit upon it, He said: Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward unto the age! And immediately the fig tree withered away.[^186] Now the fig tree signifies the Jewish synagogue, upon which the Savior found not the fitting fruit, but only the shadow of the Law; and this He took away from them, leaving it entirely destitute. items.english_text: As Thou wentest, O Lord, to Thy voluntary Passion, Thou didst say unto the Apostles on the way: "Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man shall be delivered up, as it is written of Him." Come therefore, we also, with cleansed minds, let us journey with Him and be crucified with Him, and let us mortify ourselves for His sake unto the pleasures of life, that we may also live with Him, and hear Him crying aloud: "No longer do I go unto the earthly Jerusalem to suffer, but I ascend unto My Father and your Father, and unto My God and your God, and I shall exalt you into the Jerusalem on high, into the Heavenly Kingdom!" *(Twice.)*[^192]

items.english_text: O Lord, going to Thy Passion, confirming Thine own Disciples, Thou didst say, having taken them aside: "How is it that ye remember not My words which I spoke unto you before? For it is not written that any Prophet should be slain except in Jerusalem. Now therefore the time is at hand of which I told you: for behold, I am delivered into the hands of sinners to be mocked, who also, nailing Me upon the Cross and delivering Me to burial, shall account Me loathsome as a dead man. Yet take courage: for on the third day I shall rise again, unto the joy of the faithful and life eternal!"

items.slavonic_text: Подоба́етъ вѣ́дати ка́кѡ чте́тся Те́тро Е҆ѵа́лїе. Е҆́же ѿ Матѳе́а Е҆ѵа́лїе чте́тся на два Чте́нїя все. Та́коже и҆ ѿ Ма́рка все на два. Е҆́же ѿ Лꙋкѝ чте́тся на г҃ чте́нїа. Е҆́же ѿ І҆ѡа́нна чте́тся до начала сты́хъ стра́стїи, на два Чте́нїя: до Нн҃ѣ просла́вися. Чтꙋ́тся же Е҆ѵа́лїа в три дни, въ Пн҃длокъ, въ Вто́рокъ, въ Сре́дꙋ же конча́ется на Часѣ́хъ.
items.english_text: May Christ our true God, Who came to His voluntary Passion, through the prayers of His most pure Mother and of all the saints... *This Dismissal is said on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and on Great Friday.*

items.slavonic_text: И҆ а҆́бїе начина́емъ ѕ҃ Ча́съ. Прїидѣ́те поклони́мся: г҃. и҆ ѱалмы̀ ѡ҆бы́чныѧ. Ка́ѳїсмꙋ рядовꙋ́ю. Та́же Тропа́рь, въ Ше́стый дне́ же и҆ ча́съ. И҆ Бг҃ородиченъ. ꙗ҆́кѡ не и҆́мамы дерзнове́нїа. И҆ Покло́ны, г҃. Та́же Тропа́рь, Гла́съ, в҃. Дꙋше́ю съкрꙋше́ною припа́даемъ тебѣ̀, и҆ мо́лимтися Сп҃се мі́ра: ты бо є҆сѝ Бг҃ъ ка́ющихъся:. Сла́ва: коне́цъ. И҆ ны́нѣ: весь. Проки́менъ, Ѱало́мъ, рке. Гла́съ, д҃. Внегда̀ возврати́тъ Гдⷭ҇ь плѣ́нъ Сїѡ́нь. сті́. Тогда̀ и҆спо́лнишася ра́дости оу҆ста̀ на́ша.
items.english_text: *At the third hour of the day, the Paraecclesiarch strikes the klepalo, as is the custom; and having assembled in church, we sing the Third Hour with its Psalms and customary prostrations. Then the Troparion: "O Lord, Who didst send down Thy Most Holy Spirit..." and the Theotokion: "Thou art the vine..." and 3 Prostrations. Upon a richly adorned analogion they place the Holy Tetraevangelion, and a lighted lamp. The Deacon goes forth and censes around the whole church, and the brethren according to order. At the Sixth Hour he strikes the analogion and the Gospel only. At the Ninth Hour he censes the whole church and the brethren. And thus the Priest reads the Tetraevangelion, vested in his phelonion, all standing with uncovered heads and listening. At the conclusion of the Gospel we read the Homily of Saint Ephrem on the All-Comely Joseph. And after this we say: "Blessed is the Lord God..." and the rest. The Kontakion of the day is said: "Jacob lamented the loss of Joseph" (fol. 36). And the 15 customary prostrations.*[^195]

items.slavonic_text: Прⷪро́чества І҆езеки́илева чте́нїе. Гла́ва, а҃. Бы́сть въ тридеся́тое лѣ́то, въ четве́ртый Мц҃ъ, въ пя́тый днь Мц҃а, и҆ а҆́зъ бѣ́хъ посредѣ̀ плѣне́нїя при рѣцѣ̀ Хова́рѣ и҆ ѿверзо́шася Нб҃са, и҆ ви́дѣхъ видѣ́нїа Бж҃їа. Въ пятыи днь Мц҃а, се лѣ́то пя́тое плѣне́нїя Царя̀ І҆ѡаки́ма. И҆ бы́сть сло́во Гдⷭ҇не къ І҆езеки́їлю сы́нꙋ Вꙋзе́ю, Сщ҃енникꙋ въ земли Халде́йстѣй, при рѣцѣ̀ Хова́рѣ: и҆ бы́сть на мнѣ̀ рꙋка̀ Гдⷭ҇на. И҆ ви́дѣхъ, и҆ се Дх҃ъ въздвиза́яй исхожда́ше ѿ Сѣ́вера, и҆ ѻ҆́блакъ вели́кїи вне́мъ, и҆ свѣ́тъ ѡ҆́крестъ є҆гѡ̀, и҆ ѻ҆́гнь и҆з̾ѡблиста́ѧи. И҆ посредѣ̀ є҆гѡ̀ ꙗ҆́кѡ видѣ́нїе И҆ле́ктра посредѣ̀ ѻ҆гня̀ и҆ свѣ́тъ вне́мъ: и҆ посредѣ̀ ꙗ҆́кѡ подо́бїе четы́рехъ живо́тныхъ. И҆ сїе́ са́мое видѣ́нїе и҆́хъ, подо́бїе чл҃вка въ ни́хъ. И҆ четы́ри лица̀ є҆ди́номꙋ, и҆ четы́ри крилѣ̀ є҆ди́номꙋ. И҆ сте́гнѣ и҆́хъ пра́вѣ, и҆ перна́ты ноги и҆́хъ, и҆ и҆́скры, ꙗ҆́кѡ блиста́ющаяся мѣ́дь, и҆ легцѣ̀ крилѣ̀ и҆́хъ. И҆ рꙋка̀ чл҃чя по крила́ми и҆́хъ на четы́рехъ страна́хъ и҆́хъ, и҆ лица̀ и҆́хъ, и҆ кри́ла и҆́хъ четы́рехъ, близъ ка́ждо коє́мꙋ. И҆ лица̀ ѿ тѣ́хъ не ѡ҆браща́хꙋся внегда̀ ходи́ти и҆̀мъ, ко́ждо пря́мо лицꙋ̀ и҆́хъ хожда́хꙋ.
items.english_text: With a contrite soul we fall down before Thee, and we pray Thee, O Savior of the world: for Thou art the God of the penitent!

provenance.verbatim_source: With a contrite soul we fall down before Thee, and we pray Thee, O Savior of the world: for Thou art the God of the penitent!

items.english_text: Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was in the midst of the captivity by the river Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God. On the fifth day of the month, which was the fifth year of the captivity of King Jehoiachin, the word of the Lord came expressly unto Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans, by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was upon me. And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, and a great cloud, and a light around about it, and flashing fire. And from the midst thereof as the appearance of electrum in the midst of the fire, and light in it; and in the midst thereof as the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance: they had the likeness of a man. And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings. And their legs were straight, and their feet winged, and sparks flashing like burnished bronze, and their wings were light. And the hand of a man was under their wings on their four sides; and their faces and their wings were four, each close to the other. And their faces turned not when they went; they went every one straight forward.

items.slavonic_text: И҆ подо́бїе ли́ца и҆́хъ, лицѐ Чл҃вчее, и҆ лицѐ Лво́во ѡ҆деснꙋ́ю четы́ремъ. и҆ лицѐ Телчее ѡ҆шꙋ́юю четы́ремъ. и҆ лицѐ Ѻ҆́рла четы́ремъ. И҆ кри́ла и҆́хъ просте́рта горѣ̀ четы́ремъ. коемꙋ́ждо двѣ̀ съпря́женни дрꙋ́гъ къ дрꙋ́гꙋ. и҆ двѣ̀ покрыва́хꙋ верхо̀ тѣле́съ и҆́хъ. И҆ ко́ждо по лицꙋ̀ своемꙋ̀ и҆дя́ше, и҆́деже а҆́ще бя́ше дх҃ъ ше́ствова́ти и҆дя́хꙋ и҆ не ѡ҆браща́хꙋся. И҆ посредѣ̀ живо́тныхъ видѣ́нїе ꙗ҆́кѡ оу҆́глїа ѻ҆гня̀ горя́щагѡ, ꙗ҆́кѡ зрѣ́нїе свѣ́щъ съѡбраща́ющїяся посредѣ̀ живо́тныхъ, и҆ свѣ́тъ ѻ҆гня̀, и҆ ѿ ѻ҆гня̀ и҆схожда́ше ꙗ҆́кѡ мо́лнїя. И҆ живо́тнаѧ теча́хꙋ и҆ възвраща́хꙋся, ꙗ҆́кѡ видѣ́нїе Безекъ. И҆ ви́дѣхъ, и҆ се ко́ло є҆ди́но на Землѝ держа́щееся живо́тныхъ четы́рехъ. И҆ видѣ́нїе коле́съ и҆ сътворе́нїе и҆́хъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ видѣ́нїе Ѳарси́съ, и҆ подо́бїе въ четы́рехъ, и҆ видѣ́нїа и҆́хъ и҆ дѣ́ло и҆́хъ бя́ше ꙗ҆́коже а҆́ще бы бы́ло ко́ло во колесѝ. На четы́ри страны и҆́хъ ше́ствова́хꙋ, не ѡ҆браща́хꙋся внегда̀ ше́ствовати и҆̀мъ, ни́же плещи и҆́хъ. и҆ высота̀ бя́ше и҆̀мъ. и҆ ви́дѣхъ та, и҆ плещи и҆́хъ и҆спо́лнь ѡ҆́чесъ ѡ҆́крестъ четы́ремъ. И҆ внегда̀ ше́ствовати живо́тнымъ, ше́ствова́хꙋ и҆ коле́са держа́щеся и҆́хъ, и҆ внегда̀ въздви́знꙋтися живо́тнымъ ѿ землѝ, въздвиза́хꙋся и҆ коле́са. И҆́деже а҆́ще бя́ше ѻ҆́блакъ, та́мо бя́ше и҆ дх҃ъ, є҆́же ше́ствова́ти: ше́ствова́хꙋ и҆ живо́тнаѧ, и҆ коле́са въздвиза́хꙋся сни́ми. Зане́же дх҃ъ жи́зни бя́ше въ коле́сѣхъ:. Проки́менъ. Ѱало́мъ, ркѕ. items.english_text: And as for the likeness of their faces, they four had the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right side; and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; and they four had the face of an eagle. And their wings were stretched upward; two wings of every one were joined one to another, and two covered the upper part of their bodies. And they went every one straight forward: whither the spirit was to go, they went; and they turned not as they went. And in the midst of the living creatures was an appearance like burning coals of fire, and like the appearance of lamps turning among the living creatures; and the fire was bright, and out of the fire went forth lightning. And the living creatures ran and returned, as the appearance of a flash of lightning. And I looked, and, behold, one wheel upon the earth beside the four living creatures. And the appearance of the wheels and their workmanship was as the appearance of chrysolite; and they four had one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel. When they went, they went upon their four sides: and they turned not when they went, nor their backs; and they were of lofty height; and I beheld them, and their backs were full of eyes round about them four. And when the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up. Whithersoever the cloud was, thither was the spirit to go: the living creatures went, and the wheels were lifted up with them; for the spirit of life was in the wheels.[^197]

Прїиди́те оу҆́бѡ и҆ мы̀, ѡ҆чище́ными смы́слы, сше́ствꙋимъ є҆мꙋ̀ и҆ сраспни́мсѧ, и҆ оу҆мертви́мся є҆гѡ̀ ра́ди жите́йскимъ сла́стемъ, да и҆ соживе́мъ сни́мъ, и҆ оу҆слы́шимъ
items.english_text: *The Priest having given the blessing, we say: Amen. "Come, let us worship..." (3 times). Then Psalm 103: "Bless the Lord, O my soul..." Glory... Both now... Alleluia (3 times). items.english_text: As Thou wentest, O Lord, to Thy voluntary Passion, Thou didst say unto the Apostles on the way: "Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man shall be delivered up, as it is written of Him." Come therefore, we also, with cleansed minds, let us journey with Him and be crucified with Him, and let us mortify ourselves for His sake unto the pleasures of life, that we may also live with Him, and hear Him crying aloud: "No longer do I go unto the earthly Jerusalem to suffer, but I ascend unto My Father and your Father, and unto My God and your God, and I shall exalt you into the Jerusalem on high, into the Heavenly Kingdom!" *(Twice.)*

items.english_text: Having attained, O ye faithful, unto the saving Passion of Christ God, let us glorify His ineffable longsuffering, that by His tender compassion He may also raise up us who were slain by sin, as He is good and the Lover of mankind! *(Twice.)*

items.english_text: O Lord, unto the ineffable mystery of Thy dispensation, the mother of the sons of Zebedee, not comprehending, asked of Thee to grant unto her children the honor of a temporal kingdom; but instead of this, Thou didst promise unto Thy friends to drink the cup of death, which cup Thou didst say that Thou Thyself wouldst drink before this, for the cleansing of sins. Therefore we cry aloud unto Thee: O Salvation of our souls, glory be to Thee! *(Twice.)*

items.english_text: O Lord, teaching Thine own Disciples to meditate on more perfect things, Thou didst tell them not to be like the Gentiles in exercising dominion over the lesser. "For it shall not be so with you, My Disciples, for of My own will I am poor. Let the first among you therefore be the servant of all; and he that rules, as he that is ruled; and the foremost, as the last. For I Myself am come to serve the impoverished Adam, and to give My life as a ransom for many, who cry unto Me: Glory be to Thee!" *(Twice.)*

items.english_text: O Lord, going to Thy Passion, confirming Thine own Disciples, Thou didst say, having taken them aside: "How is it that ye remember not My words which I spoke unto you before? For it is not written that any Prophet should be slain except in Jerusalem. Now therefore the time is at hand of which I told you: for behold, I am delivered into the hands of sinners to be mocked, who also, nailing Me upon the Cross and delivering Me to burial, shall account Me loathsome as a dead man. Yet take courage: for on the third day I shall rise again, unto the joy of the faithful and life eternal!"

items.english_text: These are the names of the sons of Israel who went down into Egypt together with Jacob their father; each entered with his whole household: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah; Issachar, Zebulun, Benjamin; Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. Now Joseph was already in Egypt. And all the souls that came out of Jacob were seventy-five. And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation. And the children of Israel grew and multiplied, and abounded and waxed exceedingly strong; and the land multiplied them. And there arose another king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph. And he said unto his people: "Behold, the race of the children of Israel is a great multitude, and is stronger than we. Come therefore, let us deal craftily with them, lest they multiply; and if war happen to befall us, they also join themselves unto our enemies, and having fought against us, depart out of our land." And he set over them taskmasters over their works, to afflict them in their works; and they built three strong cities for Pharaoh: Pithom, and Rameses, and On, which is Heliopolis. But the more they afflicted them, so much the more they multiplied, and waxed exceedingly strong. And the Egyptians abhorred the children of Israel, and violently oppressed the sons of Israel with force. And they made their life bitter with hard works, in clay and in brick-making, and in all manner of service in the fields, according to all their works wherein they made them serve with violence. And the King of Egypt spoke unto the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the second Puah; and he said unto them: "When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and they are about to be delivered: if it be a male child, kill him; but if it be a female, preserve her."

items.slavonic_text: бя́ше въ Е҆гѵ́птѣ. Бя́ше же всѣ́хъ дꙋ́шъ и҆з̾ше́дшихъ и҆з̾ І҆а́кѡва седмедся́тъ и҆ пя́ть. Сконча́ся же І҆ѡ́сифъ, и҆ вся Бра́тїа є҆гѡ̀, и҆ весь ро́дъ ѻ҆́ный. Сы́нове же І҆сра́илевы възрасто́ша и҆ оу҆мно́жишася, и҆ дово́лни бы́ша и҆ оу҆крѣпи́шася зѣлѡ̀ зѣлѡ̀. оу҆мно́жи же и҆̀хъ земля̀. Въста́ же Ца́рь и҆ны́й въ Е҆гѵ́птѣ, и҆́же не зна́ше І҆ѡ́сифа. Рече́ же ꙗ҆зы́кꙋ своемꙋ̀: се ꙗ҆зы́къ сынѡ́въ І҆сраилевыхъ вели́кое мно́жество, и҆ оу҆крѣпля́ется па́че на́съ. Прїидѣ́те оу҆́бѡ и҆ препремꙋдри́мъ и҆̀хъ, да некогда̀ оу҆мно́жатся, и҆ внегда̀ а҆́ще приклꙋчи́тся на́мъ бра́нь, приложа́тся и҆ ти́и къ сꙋпоста́тѡмъ и҆ и҆зратова́вше на́съ, и҆зы́дꙋтъ и҆з̾ земли на́шея. И҆ пристави́ и҆̀мъ насто́ятеля ѡ҆ дѣ́лѣхъ, да ѡ҆злоба́тъ и҆̀хъ въ дѣ́лѣхъ: и҆ съсозда́ша три гра́ды тве́рды Фараѡ́нꙋ, Пиѳѡ́мъ, и҆ Рамессѝ, и҆ Ѻ҆́нъ, є҆́же є҆́стъ И҆лїо́поль. Поели́кꙋ же и҆̀хъ смиря́хꙋ, толи́кѡ множа́йшїи быва́хꙋ, и҆ крѣпля́хꙋся зѣлѡ̀ зѣлѡ̀. И҆ ѡ҆мерзи́шася Е҆гѵптя́не ѡ҆ сынѡ́въ І҆сраилевыхъ, и҆ насили́твовахꙋ сынобо́мъ І҆сраилевомъ нꙋ́жею. И҆ болѣ́зненꙋ тѣ́мъ жи́знь творя́хꙋ, въ дѣ́лехъ жесто́кихъ, бре́нїемъ и҆ пли́нѳами, и҆ всѣ́ми дѣ́лы ꙗ҆́же въ поля́хъ. по всѣ́хъ дѣ́лехъ и҆́миже порабоща́хꙋ и҆̀хъ съ нꙋ́ждею. И҆ рече́ Ца́рь Е҆гѵ́петскїй, Ба́бамъ Е҆вре́йскимъ, є҆ди́нои и҆́мя бѣ̀ Сепфо́ра, и҆ и҆́мя второ́й Фꙋа̀. И҆ речѐ и҆̀мъ, е҆гда̀ ба́бите Е҆врея́нинамъ, и҆ бꙋ́тъ къ рожде́нїю. а҆́ще оу҆́бѡ мꙋ́жескїй по́лъ бꙋ́детъ, оу҆бива́йте и҆̀. а҆́ще ли же́нскїй по́лъ снабдѣва́йте и҆̀.
items.english_text: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the King of Egypt commanded them, but preserved the male children alive. And the King of Egypt called for the midwives, and said unto them: "Why have ye done this thing, and preserved the male children alive?" And the midwives said unto Pharaoh: "The Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they give birth before the midwives can come in unto them, and they were already delivered." Therefore God dealt well with the midwives; and the people multiplied, and waxed exceedingly strong.

items.slavonic_text: І҆́ѡва чте́нїе. Гла́ва, а҃. Мꙋ́жъ нѣ́кїй бя́ше въ страна́хъ А҆ѵсїти́йскихъ, є҆мꙋ́же и҆́мя І҆́ѡвъ. И҆ бѣ́сть чл҃къ то́й непоро́чный, пра́вный, и҆́стинный, Бг҃очести́вый, и҆ оу҆даля́яися ѡ҆ вся́кїя лꙋка́выя ве́щи. Бы́ша же є҆мꙋ̀ сынѡ́ве се́дмъ, и҆ дще́ри три. И҆ бѣ́хꙋ ско́ти є҆гѡ̀, ѡ҆ве́цъ се́дмь ты́сящїй: велблю́дъ три ты́сящи: сꙋпрꙋ́гъ воло́въ пя́ть со́тъ, и҆ ѻ҆сля́тъ же́нска по́лꙋ пасо́мыхъ пя́ть со́тъ: и҆ слꙋже́нїе мно́гое зѣлѡ̀, и҆ дѣ́ла ве́лїя бя́хꙋ є҆мꙋ̀ на землѝ. И҆ бя́ше чл҃къ ѻ҆́нъ бл҃горо́дный ѿ восто́къ со́лнца. Сходя́щежеся сынѡ́ве є҆гѡ̀ дрꙋ́гъ къ дрꙋ́гꙋ, творя́хꙋ пи́тїе на вся́кїй дн҃ь, съпосыла́юще вкꙋ́пѣ и҆ три сестры̀ своя̀, ꙗ҆́сти и҆ пи́ти с ни́ми. И҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ оу҆́бѡ скончава́шася дні́е пи́тїя, посыла́ше І҆́ѡвъ и҆ ѡ҆чища́ше и҆̀хъ въста́ющихъ оу҆́тро, и҆ приноша́ше же́ртвы ѡ҆ ни́хъ по числꙋ̀ и҆́хъ. и҆ телца́ є҆ди́ного
items.english_text: There was a certain man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was blameless, upright, true, godly, and abstaining from every evil deed. And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters. And his cattle were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she-asses feeding; and he had a very great household, and great works upon the earth; and that man was noble from the rising of the sun. And his sons went and feasted one with another, making a banquet every day, sending also for their three sisters to eat and drink with them. And when the days of their feasting were completed, Job sent and purified them, rising up early in the morning, and offered sacrifices for them according to their number, and one calf for sin for their souls. For Job said: "Lest perhaps my sons have thought evil in their hearts toward God." Thus did Job all their days. And the day came, and, behold, the Angels of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and the devil came also with them. And the Lord said unto the devil: "Whence comest thou?" And the devil answered the Lord and said: "Having gone round about the earth, and walked under heaven, I am come." And the Lord said unto him: "Hast thou considered in thy mind My servant Job? For there is none like him upon the earth, a man blameless, upright, true, godly, abstaining from every evil deed." And the devil answered and said before the Lord: "Doth Job revere God for nought? Hast Thou not made a hedge about him, and about his house within and without, and about all that he hath round about? And Thou hast blessed the works of his hands, and multiplied his cattle upon the earth. But put forth Thine hand and touch all that he hath, and see if he will not bless Thee to Thy face!" Then the Lord said unto the devil: "Behold, all that he hath I give into thine hand; only touch not himself." And the devil went out from the presence of the Lord.

items.slavonic_text: ѡ҆ грѣсѣ̀ ѡ҆ дꙋша́хъ и҆́хъ. Глаго́лаше бо І҆́ѡвъ, є҆гда̀ когда̀ сынѡ́ве моѝ въ срⷣцахъ свои́хъ зла́я помы́слиша къ Бг҃ꙋ. Си́це творя́ше І҆́ѡвъ по вся дни и҆́хъ. И҆ бы́сть дн҃ь то́й. И҆ се прїидо́ша А҆́ггли Бж҃їи ста́ти пре́ Гдⷭ҇емъ. и҆ дїа́волъ прїи́де с ни́ми. И҆ речѐ Гдⷭ҇ь дїа́волꙋ, ѿкꙋ́дꙋ прише́лъ є҆сѝ; и҆ ѿвѣща́въ дїа́волъ Гдⷭ҇ви речѐ, ѡ҆бше́дъ зе́млю и҆ проше́дъ поднебе́снꙋю, прїидо́хъ. И҆ речѐ є҆мꙋ̀ Гдⷭ҇ь: вня́лъ ли є҆сѝ мы́слїю твое́ю на раба̀ моего̀ І҆́ѡва; ꙗ҆́кѡ нѣ́сть подо́бный є҆мꙋ̀ ѿ сꙋ́щихъ на землѝ человѣ́кѡвъ, непоро́чный, пра́вный, и҆́стинный, Бг҃очести́вый. оу҆даля́яися ѡ҆ вся́кїя лꙋка́выя ве́щи. Ѿвѣща̀ дїа́волъ и҆ речѐ пре́ Гдⷭ҇емъ: е҆да̀ тꙋ́не І҆́ѡвъ чте́тъ Бг҃а; Не ты́ ли ѡ҆гради́лъ є҆сѝ є҆мꙋ̀ внꙋ́тренняя и҆ внѣ́шняя до́мꙋ є҆гѡ̀; и҆ всѣ́хъ сꙋ́щихъ є҆мꙋ̀ ѡ҆́крестъ; дѣла́ же рꙋ́кꙋ є҆го̀ бл҃гослови́лъ є҆сѝ; и҆ ско́ты є҆гѡ̀ мно́ги сътвори́лъ є҆сѝ на землѝ; Но послѝ рꙋ́кꙋ твою̀ и҆ косни́ся всѣ́хъ и҆̀хже и҆́матъ, а҆́ще не въ лице́ тя бл҃гослови́тъ. Тогда̀ речѐ Гдⷭ҇ь дїа́волꙋ: се вся є҆ли́ка сꙋ́ть є҆мꙋ̀, даю̀ въ рꙋ́кꙋ твою̀. но сама́го да некосне́шися. И҆ и҆зы́йде дїа́волъ ѿ лица̀ Гдⷭ҇ня:.

items.slavonic_text: Зрѝ: На Тра́пезѣ же, я҆́мы сꙋхояде́нїе, и҆ Си́мъ оу҆доволя́емся. И҆ ꙗ҆́коже въ Пе́рвꙋю Нд҃лю ст҃агѡ сегѡ̀ По́ста. си́це всѧ дни сїя Вели́кїй Пн҃длокъ, въ Вто́рникъ, и҆ въ Сре́дꙋ. Пости́ти подоба́етъ. Вѣ́дати подоба́етъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ Ше́стый вели́кїй Сꙋбо́ръ повелѣ̀ ст҃ы́ми строи́телми, въ По́стъ Мл҃твы и҆ оу҆миле́нїя сꙋгꙋ́бо твари́ти вѣ́рны. въ Полꙋно́щны же Вели́кїя Сꙋбѡ́ты ѡ҆ставля́ти по́стъ. Бж҃твеннымъ Е҆ѵа́гглистомъ Матѳе́ю и҆ Лꙋцѣ̀, Ѻ҆́вомꙋ оу҆́бѡ По́здѣ въ сꙋбѡ́тꙋ глаго́лющемъ, Ѻ҆во́мꙋ же Оу҆́тромъ глубо́комъ медля́емое на́мъ но́щи написа́ющимъ.

items.english_text: *Troparion 5:* Hide not in the earth the talent given unto thee, O my soul, that thou mayest repay the debt unto Christ with interest!

items.english_text: *Troparion 6:* Honor the prudent servants today; work unceasingly the secret labor of incorruptible life!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Востани́те, Жени́хъ приближа́ется. оу҆готови́мся про́чее, черто́гъ бо ѿве́рзеся. кто̀ оу҆́бѡ досто́инъ, да вни́детъ:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 7:* Arise, the Bridegroom draws near! Let us make ourselves ready henceforth, for the bridal chamber is opened: let him therefore that is worthy enter!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Оу҆краше́нъ нб҃ный черто́гъ, нн҃ѣ гото́вится, въ нетлѣ́нный невѣ́стникъ хотя́щїи вни́ти:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 8:* The heavenly chamber is adorned and made ready now for those who desire to enter into the incorruptible bridal chamber!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Помина́й мꙋ́дрыя Дв҃ы дꙋшѐ, помина́й, да съ Хрⷭ҇томъ вни́деши, въ черто́гъ свѣ́тлѡ:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 9:* Remember the wise virgins, O my soul, remember, that with Christ thou mayest enter radiantly into the bridal chamber!

provenance.verbatim_source:

Remember the wise virgins, O my soul, remember, that with Christ thou mayest enter radiantly into the bridal chamber!

items.office: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.section: At the Aposticha, Stichera Idiomela, Tone 5
items.season_or_tone: PART I: LAZARUS SATURDAY, PALM SUNDAY, AND GREAT AND HOLY PASSION WEEK
items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Ви́дите ви́дите ꙗ҆́кѡ а҆́зъ є҆́смь Бг҃ъ, и҆́же пре́жде бытїя̀ всѣ́хъ, и҆ пре́жде сътворе́нїя Землѝ и҆ нб҃а, всѣ́мъ вся, и҆́же сы́и въ Ѻ҆ц҃и, и҆ всего̀ ношя̀ всебѣ̀:.
items.english_text: See, see that I am God, Who of old led Israel through the Red Sea, and saved him, and nourished him, and delivered him from the servitude of Pharaoh!

provenance.verbatim_source: See, see that I am God, Who of old led Israel through the Red Sea, and saved him, and nourished him, and delivered him from the servitude of Pharaoh!

items.office: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.section: At the Aposticha, Stichera Idiomela, Tone 5
items.season_or_tone: PART I: LAZARUS SATURDAY, PALM SUNDAY, AND GREAT AND HOLY PASSION WEEK
items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Сло́вомъ съста́вихъ Нб҃о вкꙋ́пѣ и҆ Зе́млю, съ Ѻ҆тце́мъ во вкꙋ́пѣ, и҆ Сло́вомъ ношя́ вся, ꙗ҆́кѡ Сло́во, мꙋ́дрость, и҆ Си́ла, и҆ Ѡ҆́бразъ, и҆ съдѣ́йствителенъ и҆ равнодѣ́теленъ:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 10:* See, see that I am God, Who was before the existence of all things, and before the creation of earth and heaven, all things unto all, Who am in the Father and bear all things in Myself![^204]

provenance.verbatim_source:

See, see that I am God, Who was before the existence of all things, and before the creation of earth and heaven, all things unto all, Who am in the Father and bear all things in Myself![^204]

items.office: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.section: At the Aposticha, Stichera Idiomela, Tone 5
items.season_or_tone: PART I: LAZARUS SATURDAY, PALM SUNDAY, AND GREAT AND HOLY PASSION WEEK
items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Кто̀ вре́мена положѝ; кто̀ вѣ́ки ѡ҆блида́яй; кто̀ вся ѡ҆предѣля́яй и҆ ѡ҆бязꙋ́яй; ра́вѣ безнача́льный при́снѡ сы́и съ Ѻ҆це́мъ, ꙗ҆́коже заря̀ въ свѣ́тѣ:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 11:* By My Word I framed the heaven together with the earth, together with the Father, and by My Word I uphold all things: as Word, Wisdom, Power, Image, co-working and equal in operation!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.slavonic_text: Ѡ҆ безмѣ́рномꙋ ти чл҃колю́бїю І҆и҃се! Сказа́лъ бо є҆сѝ на́мъ сконча́нїя Сбы́ше вре́мя, съкры́въ ча́съ, оу҆чени́кѡвъ же свѣ́тлѡ ѡ҆бразы є҆гѡ̀:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 12:* Who appointed the seasons? Who rules the ages? Who determines and binds all things? The Co-beginningless, Who is ever with the Father, as the ray in the light!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.office: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.section: At the Aposticha, Stichera Idiomela, Tone 5
items.season_or_tone: PART I: LAZARUS SATURDAY, PALM SUNDAY, AND GREAT AND HOLY PASSION WEEK
items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Вся зна́еши, вся вѣ́си І҆и҃се, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆мѣ́яй все въ себѣ̀ Ѻ҆́тчее достоѧ́нїе Бж҃їи, и҆ всего̀ Дх҃а бл҃же́нна нося́и въ себѣ̀, съприрѡ́днаго Ѻ҆ц҃ꙋ̀:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 13:* O Thine immeasurable love for mankind, O Jesus! For Thou hast declared unto us the time of the end that shall come to pass, concealing the hour, yet radiantly revealing its signs unto the Disciples!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.section: At the Aposticha, Stichera Idiomela, Tone 5

items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Е҆́и Гдⷭ҇и, въ вѣ́кѡвъ тво́рче, сподо́би и҆ на́съ оу҆слы́шати тогѡ̀ гла́са, зовꙋ́щїи и҆збра́нныя Ѻ҆ц҃а, въ црⷵтво нб҃ное:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 14:* Thou knowest all things, Thou understandest all things, O Jesus, as having in Thyself the whole Fatherly divine possession, and bearing in Thyself the whole blessed Spirit, consubstantial with the Father!

items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Сла́ва: Безнача́льная, несозда́нная Трⷵце, нераздѣ́льная Е҆ди́нице, тро́е сꙋ́щая є҆ди́но, Ѻ҆́че Сн҃е и҆ Дшѐ, Е҆ди́ный Бж҃е, прїимѝ пѣ́нїе ѿ бре́нныхъ ꙗ҆зы́къ, ꙗ҆́коже ѡ҆ оу҆́стъ пла́менныхъ:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 15:* Yea, O Lord, Creator of the ages, vouchsafe that we also may hear that voice calling the chosen of the Father into the Heavenly Kingdom!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.season_or_tone: PART I: LAZARUS SATURDAY, PALM SUNDAY, AND GREAT AND HOLY PASSION WEEK
items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Сѣда́ленъ. Гла́съ, в҃. По́: Мл҃рдїя: Мл҃рдиемъ дви́жимъ Хе҃, во́лею прїи́деши стра́сти Бл҃года́телю, хотя́и страстьмѝ на́съ свободи́ти, и҆ є҆́же въ а҆́дѣ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїя. Тѣ́мже чтⷵнаѧ твоя̀ въспѣва́емъ стра́стїя, и҆ сла́вимъ сп҃се кра́инее твоѐ є҆́си съхожде́нїе:.
items.english_text: O unoriginate, uncreated Trinity, undivided Unity, Three being One, Father, Son, and Spirit, One God: receive a hymn from earthen tongues, as from flaming lips!

provenance.verbatim_source: O unoriginate, uncreated Trinity, undivided Unity, Three being One, Father, Son, and Spirit, One God: receive a hymn from earthen tongues, as from flaming lips!

items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Вся́кѡ слы́шала є҆сѝ дꙋшѐ, ка́ко Хс҃ Бж҃твенны Оу҆́чнки свои́хъ провозглаша́ше гла̀ кончи́нꙋ. разꙋмѣ́вши же тво́й коне́цъ, оу҆гото́вися про́чее, вре́мя и҆схо́да прїи́де.
items.english_text: Thou hast been revealed as a holy tabernacle, O Virgin Mother of God; for into thee the Heavenly King, having entered in the flesh, came forth radiant, fashioning man in Himself unto God!

provenance.verbatim_source: Thou hast been revealed as a holy tabernacle, O Virgin Mother of God; for into thee the Heavenly King, having entered in the flesh, came forth radiant, fashioning man in Himself unto God!

items.english_text: *Sessional Hymn, Tone 2, Podoben: "Compassion" (Милосе́рдїя):* Moved with compassion, O Christ our Benefactor, Thou comest willingly to Thy Passion, desiring by Thy suffering to deliver us from passions and from the condemnation in Hades: therefore we praise Thy venerable Passions, and we glorify Thy supreme condescension, O Savior![^205]

items.english_text: *Troparion 1:* In every way thou hast heard, O my soul, how Christ proclaimed the end unto His divine Disciples: understanding therefore thine own end, make ready henceforth, for the time of departure is come![^206]

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Позна́ла є҆сѝ непло́днаѧ дꙋшѐ, лꙋка́вагѡ раба̀ при́тчꙋ, бо́йся и҆ не небрежѝ ѡ҆ дарова́нїи є҆го́же прїя́ла є҆сѝ, да не съкры́вши въ землѝ, но да кꙋ́пли дѣ́еши:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 2:* Thou hast known, O barren soul, the parable of the wicked servant: fear, and neglect not the gift which thou hast received, lest thou hide it in the earth, but trade therewith!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.office: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.season_or_tone: PART I: LAZARUS SATURDAY, PALM SUNDAY, AND GREAT AND HOLY PASSION WEEK
items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Чл҃ческое житїѐ, пꙋтѝ и҆ то́ржествꙋ оу҆подо́бися: ты̀ оу҆́бѡ дꙋшѐ моя̀ въ си́хъ ходя́щи, приѡбрѧ́щи нѣ́что, и҆ стяжѝ съкро́вище некра́домое, добродѣ́телїи бога́тство:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 3:* Human life is likened unto a way and a fair: thou therefore, O my soul, walking in these, acquire something, and gain a treasure that cannot be stolen, the wealth of virtues!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion 3:*
Human life is likened unto a way and a fair: thou therefore, O my soul, walking in these, acquire something, and gain a treasure that cannot be stolen, the wealth of virtues!

items.office: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.season_or_tone: PART I: LAZARUS SATURDAY, PALM SUNDAY, AND GREAT AND HOLY PASSION WEEK
items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Да оу҆ясни́тся свѣща̀, да прїи́лется к се́и и҆ є҆ле́й, ꙗ҆́коже дѣ́ламъ тогда̀ състрада́нїе, да ѡ҆брѧ́щеши дꙋшѐ моя̀ черто́гъ Хв҃ъ тогда̀ ѿве́рстый:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 4:* Let the lamp be made bright, and let oil be added thereto—even compassion accompanying works—that thou, O my soul, mayest then find the bridal chamber of Christ opened!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion 4:*
Let the lamp be made bright, and let oil be added thereto—even compassion accompanying works—that thou, O my soul, mayest then find the bridal chamber of Christ opened!

items.office: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.season_or_tone: PART I: LAZARUS SATURDAY, PALM SUNDAY, AND GREAT AND HOLY PASSION WEEK
items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Въ сꙋббѡ́тꙋ бѣ́гство и҆ въ зимѣ̀, гла̀ Оу҆чи́тель седма́гѡ вѣ́ка, ско́рꙋ прегада́телствꙋетъ нн҃ѣшнагѡ вѣ́ка, въ не́мже на́иде ꙗ҆́кѡ зима̀ кончи́на.
items.english_text: *Troparion 5:* "Flight on the Sabbath and in winter," said the Teacher, predicting the speedy end of this present seventh age, wherein the end shall come like winter!

provenance.verbatim_source:

"Flight on the Sabbath and in winter," said the Teacher, predicting the speedy end of this present seventh age, wherein the end shall come like winter!

items.office: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.season_or_tone: PART I: LAZARUS SATURDAY, PALM SUNDAY, AND GREAT AND HOLY PASSION WEEK
items.day_or_date: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.slavonic_text: Ꙗ҆́кѡ ско́рость а҆́ки мо́лнїя преходя́щая: та́кѡ бꙋ́детъ стра́шное ѻ҆́ное, бл҃ки твоегѡ̀ прише́ствїе дꙋшѐ моя̀: слы́шавши оу҆́бѡ, гото́ва про́чее бы́ти потщи́ся:.
items.english_text: *Troparion 6:* Like the speed of passing lightning: so shall that fearful coming of thy Master be, O my soul! Having heard this, therefore, make haste to be ready henceforth!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion 6:*
Like the speed of passing lightning: so shall that fearful coming of thy Master be, O my soul! Having heard this, therefore, make haste to be ready henceforth!

items.office: Great and Holy Monday: Great Compline
items.season_or_tone: PART I: LAZARUS SATURDAY, PALM SUNDAY, AND GREAT AND HOLY PASSION WEEK

При Крⷵтѣ̀ твое́мъ Сп҃се, предстоя́щи Мт҃и, и҆ твоѐ непра́ведное зря́щи заколе́нїе вопїя́ше, оу҆вы̀ мнѣ̀ ча́до моѐ! оу҆вы̀ мнѣ̀, незаходи́мый Свѣ́те! просїя́й всѣ́мъ Сл҃нце Сла́вы свѣ́тъ:. Сла́ва: Е҆ди́нице ст҃а́я, Тр҃це є҆ди́но Бж҃тво, и҆ Тр҃це Е҆ди́нице Бж҃е, трїѷпоста́вное Е҆стество̀, є҆ди́но чт҃ная и҆ нераздѣли́мая Сла́во, и҆зба́ви ѿ бѣ́дъ дꙋ́ша на́ша:. И҆ ны́нѣ: Бг҃оро́диченъ. Прїимѝ Мт҃рь твою̀ Хе҃ въ мл҃твꙋ, да мл҃твами є҆я̀, оу҆мири́ши ми́ръ, и҆ оу҆тверди́ши ца́рствїя ски́птры, и҆ Цр҃кви твоя̀ совокꙋпи́ши въ є҆ди́но. И҆рмо́съ, ѳ҃. Пѣ́сни. Проявле́ннаго на горѣ̀: Зл҃. Досто́йно. И҆ покло́нъ до землѝ: Трⷵто́е: и҆ по Ѻ҆́ч҃енш҃ъ: Кꙫ: дни. лн҃тъ, м҃и. Та́же Гдⷭ҇и силъ съ на́ми бꙋ́ди. И҆ про́чее ѡ҆бы́чное. И҆ ѿпꙋ́стъ.

items.slavonic_text: Потре́бно є҆́стъ вѣ́дати, ꙗ҆́кѡ а҆́ще прилꙋчи́тся Бл҃говѣ́щенїе пр҃тыя Бц҃а въ вели́кїй Вто́рникъ. Въ Поне́дѣ́локъ ве́черъ Кади́ло, не гле́мъ. На Гдⷭ҇и въззва́хъ: Сті̑хиры самогла́сны Дни, є҆. И҆ пра́здникꙋ, є҆. Сла́ва: Гла́съ, и҆́. Вто́рꙋю Е҆ѵл҃. И҆ ны́нѣ: пра́здникꙋ. Гла́съ, ѕ҃. Посла́нъ бы́стъ. Вхо́дъ съ Е҆ѵл҃їемъ. Свѣ́те ти́хїи. Про: и҆ Чте́нїе дни, и҆ пра́: в҃. Да и҆спра́витсѧ. И҆ покло́ны, г҃. Е҆ѵл҃їе дни, и҆ про́чая Преждеѡсвѧще́нныхъ: Престаю́тъ же Покло́ны въ самы́и Ве́черни, кромѣ̀ то́чїю г҃ вели́кихъ покло́новъ. По Да и҆спра́витсѧ, и҆ по Нн҃ѣ си́лы нб҃ныя. и҆ на Бꙋ́ди и҆́мѧ Гдⷭ҇не. Та́кожде и҆ на коне́цъ Оу҆́трени, и҆ на коне́цъ Часѡ́въ, то́кмѡ вели́кихъ покло́ны, три. На Тра́пезѣ же, я҆́мы съ Е҆ле́емъ, и҆ пїемъ Вино̀. При Часѣ́ же ѕ҃мъ Но́щи кле́плетъ въ велїи тка́дло. И҆ събравшеся Пое́мъ Па́вечерни вели́кꙋю. І҆ере́й же Кади́тъ по ѡ҆бы́чаю, и҆ по Сла́ва въ вы́шнихъ, Исходи́мъ въ Притво́ръ, и҆ пое́мъ сті̑хиры самогла́сны пра: Гла́, а҆. Сла́ва: Инні́е: Бл҃говѣствꙋ́етъ Гаврїи́лъ: На сті̑: стры самогла́сны пра́: г҃. Гла́, а҆. съ сті̑хи и҆́хъ. Сла́ва, Инні́е: Гла́, то́йжде. Дне́сь ра́дость. На Бл҃женїи хлѣ́бѡвъ. Тропа́рь пра́здникꙋ, г҃. и҆ Чте́нїе Пра́здникꙋ. НА ОУ҆́ТРНИ. На Бг҃ъ Гдⷭ҇ь: Тропа́рь пра́: г҃. И҆ по ѡ҆бы́хъ Кади́мы Сѣда́лна въ трїѡди, и҆ Чте́нїе дни. По г҃ Кади́смѣ сѣда́: пра́: и҆ Чте́нїе пра́: Полиеле́осъ и҆ сѣ́да: пра: и҆ чте́нїе пра: Степе́: а҆ а҆нтїф: д҃-гѡ Гла́са. Проки́менъ. Вся́кое дыха́нїе. Е҆ѵл҃їе пра: Ѱало́мъ, н҃. съ стры пра́здникꙋ. Кано́нъ пра: съ И҆рмосо́мъ на ѕ҃. Катавасі́а пра: И҆рмо́съ ѡ҆́ба лика вкꙋ́пѣ. И҆́деже Двоєпѣ́снецъ въ трїѡди пое́мъ Кано́нъ пра́: съ И҆рмосо́мъ на ѕ҃. А҆ Двоєпѣ́снецъ на и҆́. И҆ послѣ́ди И҆рмо́съ въ трїѡди, ѡ҆ба ли́ка вкꙋ́пѣ. По г҃ пѣ́сни, Ко: дни, и҆ І҆́косъ. и҆ сѣда́: пра: и҆ Чте́нїе пра́здникꙋ. По ѕ҃ пѣ́сни, Ко: пра́з: На д҃ пѣ́сни Чтнѣ́йшꙋю непое́мъ. Свѣти́ленъ пра́здникꙋ. Сла́ва, дни. И҆ ны́нѣ, пра́: На Хвали́техъ, сті̑хиры по: пра́здникꙋ. Гла́, а҆, на д҃. Сла́ва: Гла́, в҃, дни. Ꙗ҆́кѡ дꙋшевною лѣ́ностїю. И҆ ны́нѣ, пра́здникꙋ. Е҆́же ѿ вѣ́ка та́инство. На сті̑х: самогла́сны дни, съ сті̑хи и҆́хъ. Сла́ва: пра́здникꙋ. Гла́, и҆́. Да веселя́тся нб҃са. И҆ ны́нѣ: дни, Гла́, ѕ҃. Е҆гда̀ прїи́деши. Тропа́рь пра́здникꙋ. Е҆ктени́: и҆ поклоны, г҃ вели́кихъ. Прїиди́те поклони́мся, г҃. И҆ ча́съ, а҆. на а҆мъ Часѣ́ Тропа́рь, и҆ по Ѻ҆́че на́шъ: Ко: пра́здникꙋ. На коне́цъ г҃ поклоны вели́кихъ, съ Мл҃твою. и҆ ѿпꙋ́стъ. и҆ ѡ҆бы́чное и҆схожде́нїе въ Притво́ръ. При Часѣ́ же г҃мъ дни, кле́плетъ, и҆ твори́мъ Нехожде́нїе внѣ̀ Ѡ҆би́тели. И҆ възвра́тившеся, Пое́мъ Часы̀ съ Кадїлма́ми и҆ Чте́нїе Тетро Е҆ѵл҃їе. и҆ гле́мъ на Часѣ́хъ, Тропарь, и҆ Ко: пра́здникꙋ. В ча́съ, ѳ҃. бє Ва́: и҆ бє покло́нѡвъ. Бл҃жена ско́рѡ, без̾ пѣ́нїа, и҆ Помяни́ насъ, и҆ про́чая. Ко: пра́здникꙋ. Гдⷭ҇и поми́лꙋй, м҃. и҆ покло́нѡвъ, г҃ вели́кихъ. Та́же Мл҃тва. и҆ ѿпꙋ́стъ. Та́же Начина́емъ Вечерню, въ Ка́ѳізмы, и҆ без покло́нѡвъ. На Гдⷭ҇и въззва́хъ: Стры самогла́сны Дни, на є҆. И҆ пра́: на є҆. Сла́: дни, Гла́, ѕ҃. Е҆гда̀ прии́деши. И҆ нн҃ѣ: пра: Гл: то́. Посла́нъ бы́стъ.

items.slavonic_text: ВЪ СТ҃Ы́Й И҆ ВЕЛИ́КІЙ ВТО́РНИКЪ. НА ОУ҆́ТРНИ. А҆ллилꙋ́їа, на Гла́съ, и҆́. Тропа́рь, г҃. Сежени́хъ гряде́тъ въ полꙋ́нощи. въ Пнⷣлни́къ вели́кїй. Зри Ли́стъ, л҃е. По а҃. Ка́ѳісмѣ, Сѣда́ленъ. Гла́съ, д҃. Подо́бенъ: Възнесны́йся на крⷵтъ: Жениха̀ бра́тїе възлюби́мъ, свѣщя̀ своя̀ оу҆краси́мъ, въ добродѣ́телехъ сїя́юще, и҆ вѣ́рѣ пра́вой. да ꙗ҆́кѡ мꙋ́дрыя Гдⷭ҇ня Дѣ́вы готови вни́демъ сни́мъ на бра́ки. Жени́хъ бо да́ры ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ, всѣ́мъ подае́тъ, нетлѣ́нный вѣне́цъ:. Сла́ва: И҆ ны́нѣ: то́йжде. По в҃й, Стіхоло́гїи. Сѣда́ленъ. Гла́съ, д҃. Подо́бенъ. Оу҆диви́ся І҆ѡ́сифъ: Совѣ́тъ сп҃се беззако́нный на тя, свяще́нници и҆ Кни́жници за́вистїю събра́вше лю́тѣ, къ преда́телство подвиго́ша І҆ꙋ́дꙋ. Тѣ́мже безстꙋ́днѡ и҆схожда́ше, глаго́лаша на тя беззако́ннымъ лю́демъ, что́ ми рече́ даете, и҆ а҆́зъ вамъ є҆го̀ преда́мъ въ рꙋ́ки ва́ша, ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїя сего̀ и҆зба́ви Гдⷭ҇и дꙋ́ша на́ша:. Сла́ва: И҆ ны́нѣ: то́. По г҃й Стіхоло́гїи. Сѣда́ленъ. Гла́съ, и҆́. Подо́бенъ. Премрости: І҆ꙋ́да ра́зꙋмомъ сребролю́бствꙋетъ, на Оу҆чи́теля неи́стовъ подвиза́ется, совѣ́тꙋетъ, поꙋча́ется преда́нїю, свѣ́та ѿпада́етъ тмꙋ̀ прїи́мъ: соглаша́ется цѣ́нꙋ, продае́тъ безцѣ́ннаго. тѣ́мже и҆ оу҆давле́нїе възме́здїе и҆́хже содѣ́я ѡ҆брѣта́етъ ѡ҆кая́нный, и҆ лю́тꙋю сме́рть, преда́въ тебѐ Гдⷭ҇я. Тогѡ̀ на́съ ча́сти и҆зба́ви Хе҃ Бж҃е, съгрѣше́нїемъ ѡ҆ставле́нїе да́рꙋя, пра́зднꙋющымъ любо́вїю, пречт҃ыя Стра̑сти твоя̀:. Сла́ва: И҆ ны́нѣ: то́йжде. Та́же, Ѱало́мъ, н҃. Та́же, Сп҃си Бж҃е лю́ди своя̀. Гдⷭ҇и поми́лꙋй, в҃і. Пое́мъ Дїа́конства ма́лая: Ко: гла́, в҃. По́: Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀: Ча́съ а҆́ще конца̀ помысливши, и҆ посѣче́нїа смоко́вница оу҆боя́вшися, да́нный ти тала́нтъ трꙋдолю́бнѡ дѣ́лай ѡ҆каѧ́нная, бо́дрствꙋющи и҆ зовꙋ́щи, да непребꙋ́демъ внѣ̀ черто́га Хв҃а:. І҆́косъ. Что̀ оу҆ныва́еши дꙋшѐ моя̀ ѡ҆кая́нная; что̀ мечта́еши без̾вре́меннѡ попече́нїа неполе́зная; что̀ оу҆пражня́ешися къ мимотекꙋ́щимъ; послѣ́днїи ча́съ є҆́стъ ѿсе́лѣ, и҆ разлꙋчи́тися и҆́мамы ѿ сꙋ́щихъ зде́: до́ндеже вре́мя и҆́маши, въздви́гни зовꙋ́щи: съгрѣши́хъ ти Сп҃се мо́й, непосѣци́ менѐ, ꙗ҆́коже непло́днꙋю смоко́вницꙋ. но ꙗ҆́кѡ мл҃рдъ Гдⷭ҇и, ѡ҆уще́дри со стра́хомъ зовꙋ́щымъ, да непребꙋ́демъ внѣ̀ черто́га Хв҃а:. Сѵназа́ръ, въ ст҃ыи и҆ вели́кїй вто́: Бл҃ви Ѻ҆́ч҃е. Стіхѝ: Вто́рникъ велича́йшїй Дѣ́вы де́сять носи́тъ. Побѣ́до нося́щымъ невꙋмы́тнагѡ Вл҃ки.
items.english_text: Let us love the Bridegroom, O brethren! Let us adorn our lamps, shining with virtues and orthodox faith, that like the wise virgins of the Lord we may be ready to enter with Him unto the marriage banquet: for the Bridegroom, as God, bestows upon all an incorruptible crown!

provenance.verbatim_source: Let us love the Bridegroom, O brethren! Let us adorn our lamps, shining with virtues and orthodox faith, that like the wise virgins of the Lord we may be ready to enter with Him unto the marriage banquet: for the Bridegroom, as God, bestows upon all an incorruptible crown!

items.english_text: The lawless council against Thee, O Savior, being grievously gathered together by the priests and scribes in malice, stirred up Judas unto betrayal; therefore brazenly he went forth, saying unto the lawless people: "What will ye give me, and I will deliver Him into your hands?" From this condemnation deliver our souls, O Lord!

items.english_text: Judas in his mind is overcome by the love of money; raging, he is moved against the Master; he deliberates and studies betrayal; he falls from the light, receiving darkness; he bargains the price, he sells the One Who is beyond price; therefore the wretch finds hanging as the reward for what he has done, and a bitter death, having betrayed Thee, the Lord! Deliver us from his portion, O Christ God, granting forgiveness of transgressions unto those who celebrate Thy most pure Passions with love!

Тѣ́мже безстꙋ́днѡ и҆схожда́ше, глаго́лаша на тя беззако́ннымъ лю́демъ, что́ ми рече́ даете, и҆ а҆́зъ вамъ є҆го̀ преда́мъ въ рꙋ́ки ва́ша, ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїя сего̀ и҆зба́ви Гдⷭ҇и дꙋ́ша на́ша:. Сла́ва: И҆ ны́нѣ: то́. По г҃й Стіхоло́гїи. Сѣда́ленъ. Гла́съ, и҆́. Подо́бенъ. Премрости: І҆ꙋ́да ра́зꙋмомъ сребролю́бствꙋетъ, на Оу҆чи́теля неи́стовъ подвиза́ется, совѣ́тꙋетъ, поꙋча́ется преда́нїю, свѣ́та ѿпада́етъ тмꙋ̀ прїи́мъ: соглаша́ется цѣ́нꙋ, продае́тъ безцѣ́ннаго. тѣ́мже и҆ оу҆давле́нїе възме́здїе и҆́хже содѣ́я ѡ҆брѣта́етъ ѡ҆кая́нный, и҆ лю́тꙋю сме́рть, преда́въ тебѐ Гдⷭ҇я. Тогѡ̀ на́съ ча́сти и҆зба́ви Хе҃ Бж҃е, съгрѣше́нїемъ ѡ҆ставле́нїе да́рꙋя, пра́зднꙋющымъ любо́вїю, пречт҃ыя Стра̑сти твоя̀:. Сла́ва: И҆ ны́нѣ: то́йжде. Та́же, Ѱало́мъ, н҃. Та́же, Сп҃си Бж҃е лю́ди своя̀. Гдⷭ҇и поми́лꙋй, в҃і. Пое́мъ Дїа́конства ма́лая: Ко: гла́, в҃. По́: Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀: Ча́съ а҆́ще конца̀ помысливши, и҆ посѣче́нїа смоко́вница оу҆боя́вшися, да́нный ти тала́нтъ трꙋдолю́бнѡ дѣ́лай ѡ҆каѧ́нная, бо́дрствꙋющи и҆ зовꙋ́щи, да непребꙋ́демъ внѣ̀ черто́га Хв҃а:. І҆́косъ. Что̀ оу҆ныва́еши дꙋшѐ моя̀ ѡ҆кая́нная; что̀ мечта́еши без̾вре́меннѡ попече́нїа неполе́зная; что̀ оу҆пражня́ешися къ мимотекꙋ́щимъ; послѣ́днїи ча́съ є҆́стъ ѿсе́лѣ, и҆ разлꙋчи́тися и҆́мамы ѿ сꙋ́щихъ зде́: до́ндеже вре́мя и҆́маши, въздви́гни зовꙋ́щи: съгрѣши́хъ ти Сп҃се мо́й, непосѣци́ менѐ, ꙗ҆́коже непло́днꙋю смоко́вницꙋ. но ꙗ҆́кѡ мл҃рдъ Гдⷭ҇и, ѡ҆уще́дри со стра́хомъ зовꙋ́щымъ, да непребꙋ́демъ внѣ̀ черто́га Хв҃а:. Сѵназа́ръ, въ ст҃ыи и҆ вели́кїй вто́: Бл҃ви Ѻ҆́ч҃е. Стіхѝ: Вто́рникъ велича́йшїй Дѣ́вы де́сять носи́тъ. Побѣ́до нося́щымъ невꙋмы́тнагѡ Вл҃ки.
items.english_text: If thou ponderest the hour of the end, O wretched soul, and fearest the cutting down of the fig tree: labor industriously with the talent given unto thee, watching and crying aloud: "May we not remain outside the bridal chamber of Christ!"

items.english_text: *Ikos:* Why art thou despondent, O my wretched soul? Why dost thou imagine unprofitable anxieties out of season? Why art thou occupied with passing things? The last hour is at hand, and we must depart from things present: while thou hast time, arise and cry aloud: "I have sinned against Thee, my Savior! Cut me not down like the barren fig tree; but as Thou art compassionate, O Lord, have mercy upon those who cry out with fear: May we not remain outside the bridal chamber of Christ!"

provenance.verbatim_source:

Cut me not down like the barren fig tree; but as Thou art compassionate, O Lord, have mercy upon those who cry out with fear: May we not remain outside the bridal chamber of Christ!"

items.slavonic_text: Та́же ДВОЕПѢ́СНЕЦЪ. Е҆мꙋ́же Краегране́сїе: ТРІ́ТИТЕ. Си́рѣчъ, въ вто́рникъ же. Творе́нїе Гд҃на Ко́змы, И҆рмо́съ по в҃, Стіхи́ же на ѕ҃. Послѣ́днїе И҆рмо́съ, ѡ҆ба ли́ка вкꙋ́пѣ. Гла́съ, в҃. Пѣ́нь, и҆́. И҆рмо́съ. Велѣ́нїю мꙋчи́телевꙋ, Прпⷣбныѧ три ѻ҆́кроки непови́нꙋвшеся, въ пе́щь повержени бы́вше, Бг҃а и҆сповѣ́даахꙋ пою́ще, бл҃вите дѣ́ла Гдⷭ҇а Гдⷭ҇а:. Лѣ́ность дале́че на́съ ѿве́ржемъ, и҆ свѣ́тлыми свѣща́ми безсме́ртнагѡ Жениха̀ Хрⷭ҇та̀, пѣ́нїемъ оу҆сря́щимъ, бл҃вите вопїю́ще дѣ́ла Гдⷭ҇на Гдⷭ҇а:. Да оу҆довлѣ́етъ ѡ҆бщи́телныи дꙋша на́шея є҆ле́и въ сосꙋ́дѣхъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ да не на кꙋ́пли поло́жше вре́мя поче́нтїи, пое́мъ: бл҃вите дѣ́ла Гдⷭ҇на Гдⷭ҇а: Тала́нтъ є҆ли́цы ѿ Бг҃а прїя́сте, равноси́лнꙋю бл҃гть, по́мощїи да́вшагѡ Хрⷭ҇та възрасти́те, пою́ще: бл҃гослови́те дѣ́ла Гдⷭ҇на Гдⷭ҇а:. Хва́ли бл҃ви кла́няемся Гдⷭ҇ви пое́мъ и҆ превозноси є҆го в вѣ́ки. И҆ па́ки ѡ҆ба ли́ка И҆рмо́. Велѣ́нїю мꙋчи́телевꙋ: Пѣ́нь, ѳ҃. И҆рмо́съ. Невмѣсти́маго Бг҃а, въ оу҆тро́бѣ въмѣсти́вшаѧ, и҆ ра́дость мі́рꙋ роди́вшаѧ, тебе пое́мъ Всест҃ая Дв҃о:. Оу҆чнкѡ́мъ бл҃гїи, бди́те ре́клъ є҆сѝ, во́нже бо ча́съ прїи́детъ Гдⷭ҇ь не разꙋмѣ́ете, ѿда́ти комꙋ́ждо:. Въ второ́мъ твое́мъ и҆ стра́шномъ прише́ствїи Бл҃ко, десны́мъ ѻ҆вца́мъ мя съпричтѝ, прегрѣше́нїй презрѣ́въ мои́хъ мно́жества:. И҆ па́ки възмѣ́сто Досто́йна. И҆рмо́. items.slavonic_text: Та́же ДВОЕПѢ́СНЕЦЪ. Е҆мꙋ́же Краегране́сїе: ТРІ́ТИТЕ. Си́рѣчъ, въ вто́рникъ же. Творе́нїе Гд҃на Ко́змы, И҆рмо́съ по в҃, Стіхи́ же на ѕ҃. Послѣ́днїе И҆рмо́съ, ѡ҆ба ли́ка вкꙋ́пѣ. Гла́съ, в҃. Пѣ́нь, и҆́. И҆рмо́съ. Велѣ́нїю мꙋчи́телевꙋ, Прпⷣбныѧ три ѻ҆́кроки непови́нꙋвшеся, въ пе́щь повержени бы́вше, Бг҃а и҆сповѣ́даахꙋ пою́ще, бл҃вите дѣ́ла Гдⷭ҇а Гдⷭ҇а:. Лѣ́ность дале́че на́съ ѿве́ржемъ, и҆ свѣ́тлыми свѣща́ми безсме́ртнагѡ Жениха̀ Хрⷭ҇та̀, пѣ́нїемъ оу҆сря́щимъ, бл҃вите вопїю́ще дѣ́ла Гдⷭ҇на Гдⷭ҇а:. Да оу҆довлѣ́етъ ѡ҆бщи́телныи дꙋша на́шея є҆ле́и въ сосꙋ́дѣхъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ да не на кꙋ́пли поло́жше вре́мя поче́нтїи, пое́мъ: бл҃вите дѣ́ла Гдⷭ҇на Гдⷭ҇а: Тала́нтъ є҆ли́цы ѿ Бг҃а прїя́сте, равноси́лнꙋю бл҃гть, по́мощїи да́вшагѡ Хрⷭ҇та възрасти́те, пою́ще: бл҃гослови́те дѣ́ла Гдⷭ҇на Гдⷭ҇а:. Хва́ли бл҃ви кла́няемся Гдⷭ҇ви пое́мъ и҆ превозноси є҆го в вѣ́ки. И҆ па́ки ѡ҆ба ли́ка И҆рмо́. Велѣ́нїю мꙋчи́телевꙋ: Пѣ́нь, ѳ҃. И҆рмо́съ. Невмѣсти́маго Бг҃а, въ оу҆тро́бѣ въмѣсти́вшаѧ, и҆ ра́дость мі́рꙋ роди́вшаѧ, тебе пое́мъ Всест҃ая Дв҃о:. Оу҆чнкѡ́мъ бл҃гїи, бди́те ре́клъ є҆сѝ, во́нже бо ча́съ прїи́детъ Гдⷭ҇ь не разꙋмѣ́ете, ѿда́ти комꙋ́ждо:. Въ второ́мъ твое́мъ и҆ стра́шномъ прише́ствїи Бл҃ко, десны́мъ ѻ҆вца́мъ мя съпричтѝ, прегрѣше́нїй презрѣ́въ мои́хъ мно́жества:. И҆ па́ки възмѣ́сто Досто́йна. И҆рмо́. Невмѣсти́маго Бг҃а, въ оу҆тро́бѣ: Свѣти́ленъ, г҃. Черто́гъ тво́й ви́ждꙋ сп҃се мо́й оу҆кра́шенный, и҆ ѡ҆де́жды не и҆́мамъ да вни́дꙋ во́нь, просвѣти́ ми ѡ҆дѣя́нїе дꙋшѝ свѣтода́вче и҆ сп҃си мя̀:. НА ХВАЛИ́ТЕХЪ. Поста́вимъ стіхо́въ, д҃. И҆ пое́мъ стры самогла́сны, Гла́съ, а҆. Въ свѣ́тлостехъ ст҃ы́хъ твои́хъ, ка́кѡ вни́дꙋ недосто́йныи; а҆́ще бо дерзнꙋ̀ внити въ черто́гъ, ѡ҆дѣя́нїе мя ѡ҆блича́етъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ нѣ́сть бра́чное, и҆ свя́занъ и҆згна́нъ бꙋ́дꙋ ѿ А҆́гглѡвъ. ѡ҆чи́сти Гдⷭ҇и скве́рнꙋ дꙋша моея̀, и҆ сп҃си́ мя ꙗ҆́кѡ чл҃колю́бецъ:. два́жды. Гла́съ, в҃. Дꙋше́вною лѣ́ностїю въздрѣма́вся, не стяжа́хъ Жени́ше Хрⷭ҇те, горя́ща свѣти́лника, я҆́же ѿ добродѣ́телїй, и҆ дѣ́вамъ оу҆подо́бихся бꙋи́мъ, въ вре́мя дѣла́нїя глꙋмля́ся: мл҃рдїя щедро́тъ твои́хъ не затвори́ ми Бл҃ко, но ѿтря́съ мо́й ѡ҆мраче́нныи со́нъ възста́ви, и҆ съ мꙋ́дрыми съвведи́ дѣ́вами въ черто́гъ тво́й, и҆́деже гла́съ чи́стыи
items.english_text: *Ode 9. Heirmos:* Thou who hast contained in thy womb the uncontainable God, and hast brought forth joy unto the world: we sing of thee, O All-Holy Virgin![^221]

items.english_text: Into the splendors of Thy saints, how shall I enter being unworthy? For if I dare to enter into the bridal chamber, my garment reproaches me, that it is not a wedding garment, and being bound I shall be cast out by the Angels! Cleanse, O Lord, the defilement of my soul, and save me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind! *(Twice)*

items.english_text: Slumbering in spiritual sloth, I have not acquired a burning lamp from virtues, O Bridegroom Christ, and I am likened unto the foolish virgins, wandering about in the time of labor: shut not against me the loving-kindness of Thy compassions, O Master; but having shaken off my darkened sleep, raise me up, and lead me with the wise virgins into Thy bridal chamber, where the voice of those who feast is pure where the voice of those who feast is pure, and who cry unceasingly: "Lord, glory to Thee!" *(Twice)*

items.slavonic_text: ВЪ СТ҃Ы́Й И҆ ВЕЛИ́КІЙ ВТО́РНИКЪ. На ѕ҃мъ Ча́сѣ, Тропа́рь Пррⷵчества. Гла́съ, д҃. Безмѣ́рнѡ съгрѣша́ющымъ бога́тнѡ простѝ Сп҃се, и҆ сподо́би на́съ неѡсꙋжде́ннѡ поклони́тися твое́мꙋ ст҃о́мꙋ въскрⷵнїю, мл҃твами прч҃тыя ти Мт҃ре, є҆ди́не многомл҃тиве:. Сла́ва: коне́цъ. И҆ ны́нѣ безъ. Проки́менъ. Ѱало́, рк҃д. Гла́съ, ѕ҃. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ѡ҆ Гдⷭ҇а мл҃ть, и҆ мно́гое ѡ҆ него̀ и҆збавле́нїе. Сті́: И҆з̾ глꙋбины̀ въззва́ к тебѣ̀ Гдⷭ҇и, Гдⷭ҇и оу҆слы́ши. Пррⷵчества І҆езекі́илева чте́нїе. Гла́: б. Сті́: ка́. Негда̀ ходи́ти живо́тнымъ, хожда́хꙋ и҆ колеса̀, и҆ внегда̀ стоѧ́ти и҆̀мъ, стоя́ша, и҆ внегда̀ възима́тїя и҆̀мъ ѿ земля̀, възима́хꙋся с ни́ми: ꙗ҆́кѡ дх҃ъ жи́зни бя́ше
items.english_text: Hearing the condemnation of him that hid the talent, O soul, hide not the word of God! Proclaim His marvelous works, that multiplying the gift, thou mayest enter into the joy of thy Lord!

items.english_text: Come, ye faithful, let us labor eagerly for the Master: for He distributs riches unto His servants, and according to the measure let each of us multiply the talent of grace![^223] Let one bring forth wisdom through good works; let another accomplish a radiant service; let another share the word with the untaught in the mystery; and let another distribute his wealth unto the poor: for thus we shall multiply the great reward, and as faithful stewards of grace we shall be accounted worthy of the Master's joy! Of this make us worthy, O Christ God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

items.english_text: When Thou shalt come in glory with the Angelic Hosts, and shalt sit upon the throne of judgment, O Jesus: do not separate me, O Good Shepherd! For Thou knowest the paths on the right, but crooked are those on the left: destroy me not therefore with the goats abominable in sins; but having numbered me with the sheep on the right hand, save me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

items.english_text: O Bridegroom, fairer in beauty than all the sons of men, Who hast called us unto the spiritual banquet of Thy bridal chamber: strip off the unsightly form of my sins through the communion of Thy Passions, and having adorned me with the robe of glory of Thy beauty, show me to be a radiant guest of Thy kingdom, as Thou art compassionate!

items.english_text: Behold, the Master entrusts thee with the talent, O my soul: receive the gift with fear; lend unto Him that gave it; distribute unto the poor, and acquire the Lord as a friend, that thou mayest stand on His right hand when He shall come in glory, and mayest hear the blessed voice: "Enter, good servant, into the joy of thy Lord!" Of this make me worthy, O Savior, who have gone astray, for the sake of Thy great mercy!

items.english_text: When the living creatures went, the wheels went; and when they stood, they stood; and when they were lifted up from the earth, they were lifted up with them: for the spirit of life was was in the wheels. And the likeness above the head of the living creatures was as a firmament, as the appearance of crystal, stretched out over their wings above. And under the firmament their wings were straight, trembling one toward another: each one had two joined covering their bodies. And I heard the voice of their wings when they flew, as the voice of abundant waters, as the voice of God Shaddai; when they went, the voice of speech was as the voice of a host; and when they stood, their wings ceased. And behold, there was a voice from above the firmament that was over their heads: when they stood, their wings were let down. And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone; and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it. And I saw as the appearance of amber, as the appearance of fire within it round about, from the appearance of the loins and upward; and from the appearance of the loins even downward, I saw as the appearance of fire, and the radiance round about. As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the radiance round about: this was the appearance of the likeness of the Glory of the Lord.

items.slavonic_text: ВТО́ЙЖДЕ СТ҃Ы́Й И҆ ВЕЛИ́КІЙ ВТО́РНИКЪ Ве́черъ. НА ГДⷭ҇И ВЪЗЗВА́ХЪ: Поста́ви Стіхѡвъ, г҃. и҆ пое́мъ ст҃ры самогла́сны. Гла́съ, а҆. Въ свѣ́тлостехъ ст҃ы́хъ твои́хъ, ка́кѡ вни́дꙋ недосто́йныи; а҆́ще бо дерзнꙋ̀ внити въ черто́гъ, ѡ҆дѣя́нїе мя ѡ҆блича́етъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ нѣ́сть бра́чное, и҆ свя́занъ и҆згна́нъ бꙋ́дꙋ ѿ А҆́гглѡвъ. ѡ҆чи́сти Гдⷭ҇и скве́рнꙋ дꙋша моея̀, и҆ сп҃си́ мя ꙗ҆́кѡ чл҃колю́бецъ:. два́жды. Гла́съ, в҃. Дꙋше́вною лѣ́ностїю въздрѣма́вся, не стяжа́хъ Жени́ше Хрⷭ҇те, горя́ща свѣти́лника, я҆́же ѿ добродѣ́телїй, и҆ дѣ́вамъ оу҆подо́бихся бꙋи́мъ, въ вре́мя дѣла́нїя глꙋмля́ся: мл҃рдїя щедро́тъ твои́хъ не затвори́ ми Бл҃ко, но ѿтря́съ мо́й ѡ҆мраче́нныи со́нъ възста́ви, и҆ съ мꙋ́дрыми съвведи́ дѣ́вами въ черто́гъ тво́й, и҆́деже гла́съ чи́стыи пра́зднꙋющихъ, и҆ вопїю́щихъ непреста́ннѡ, Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ́:. Гла́съ, д҃. Съкры́вшагѡ тала́нтъ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїе слы́шавши ѽ дꙋшѐ, не съкрыва́й словесѐ Бж҃їя, възвѣ́щꙋй чꙋдеса̀ є҆гѡ̀, да оу҆множа́ющи да́ръ, вни́деши въ ра́дость Гдⷭ҇а твоегѡ̀:. два́жды. Гла́съ, ѕ҃. Жени́ше добро́то́ю кра́сныи па́че всѣ́хъ чл҃вкъ, призва́выи на́съ къ Тра́пезѣ дх҃о́вной черто́га твоегѡ̀, нелѣ́пыи мо́й зра́къ прегрѣше́нїй съвлецы̀, и҆ прича́стїемъ твои́хъ Стрⷵтїй, въ ѡ҆де́ждꙋ сла́вы ѡ҆дѣ́явъ твоея̀ красоты̀, съѡбѣ́дника мя свѣ́тла покажѝ твоегѡ̀ црⷵтвїя, ꙗ҆́кѡ мл҃рдъ:. Гла́съ, ѕ҃. Прїиди́те вѣ́рнїи дѣ́лаимъ оу҆се́рдно Влⷣцѣ:
items.english_text: Into the splendors of Thy saints, how shall I enter being unworthy? For if I dare to enter into the bridal chamber, my garment reproaches me, that it is not a wedding garment, and being bound I shall be cast out by the Angels! Cleanse, O Lord, the defilement of my soul, and save me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind! *(Twice)*

Дꙋше́вною лѣ́ностїю въздрѣма́вся, не стяжа́хъ Жени́ше Хрⷭ҇те, горя́ща свѣти́лника, я҆́же ѿ добродѣ́телїй, и҆ дѣ́вамъ оу҆подо́бихся бꙋи́мъ, въ вре́мя дѣла́нїя глꙋмля́ся: мл҃рдїя щедро́тъ твои́хъ не затвори́ ми Бл҃ко, но ѿтря́съ мо́й ѡ҆мраче́нныи со́нъ възста́ви, и҆ съ мꙋ́дрыми съвведи́ дѣ́вами въ черто́гъ тво́й, и҆́деже гла́съ чи́стыи пра́зднꙋющихъ, и҆ вопїю́щихъ непреста́ннѡ, Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ́:. Гла́съ, д҃. Съкры́вшагѡ тала́нтъ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїе слы́шавши ѽ дꙋшѐ, не съкрыва́й словесѐ Бж҃їя, възвѣ́щꙋй чꙋдеса̀ є҆гѡ̀, да оу҆множа́ющи да́ръ, вни́деши въ ра́дость Гдⷭ҇а твоегѡ̀:. два́жды. Гла́съ, ѕ҃. Жени́ше добро́то́ю кра́сныи па́че всѣ́хъ чл҃вкъ, призва́выи на́съ къ Тра́пезѣ дх҃о́вной черто́га твоегѡ̀, нелѣ́пыи мо́й зра́къ прегрѣше́нїй съвлецы̀, и҆ прича́стїемъ твои́хъ Стрⷵтїй, въ ѡ҆де́ждꙋ сла́вы ѡ҆дѣ́явъ твоея̀ красоты̀, съѡбѣ́дника мя свѣ́тла покажѝ твоегѡ̀ црⷵтвїя, ꙗ҆́кѡ мл҃рдъ:. Гла́съ, ѕ҃. Прїиди́те вѣ́рнїи дѣ́лаимъ оу҆се́рдно Влⷣцѣ:
items.english_text: Slumbering in spiritual sloth, I have not acquired a burning lamp from virtues, O Bridegroom Christ, and I am likened unto the foolish virgins, wandering about in the time of labor: shut not against me the loving-kindness of Thy compassions, O Master; but having shaken off my darkened sleep, raise me up, and lead me with the wise virgins into Thy bridal chamber, where the voice of those who feast is pure, and who cry unceasingly: "Lord, glory to Thee!"

provenance.verbatim_source:
Come, ye faithful, let us labor eagerly for the Master...
...for He distributs riches unto His servants, and according to the measure let each of us multiply the talent of grace! Let one bring forth wisdom through good works; let another accomplish a radiant service; let another share the word with the untaught in the mystery; and let another distribute his wealth unto the poor: for thus we shall multiply what was lent, and as faithful stewards of grace we shall be accounted worthy of the Master's joy! Of this make us worthy, O Christ God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

items.english_text: Behold, the Master entrusts thee with the talent, O my soul: receive the gift with fear; lend unto Him that gave it; distribute unto the poor, and acquire the Lord as a friend, that thou mayest stand on His right hand when He shall come in glory, and mayest hear the blessed voice: "Enter, good servant, into the joy of thy Lord!" Of this make me worthy, O Savior, who have gone astray, for the sake of Thy great mercy!

Бы́сть ꙗ҆́кѡ де́нь се́й, сыно́ве І҆ѡ́вовы и҆ дще́ра є҆гѡ̀ пїя́хꙋ вино̀, въ домꙋ̀ бра́та своегѡ̀ старѣ́йшагѡ. items.english_text: When Thou shalt come in glory with the Angelic Hosts, and shalt sit upon the throne of judgment, O Jesus: do not separate me, O Good Shepherd! For Thou knowest the paths on the right, but crooked are those on the left: destroy me not therefore with the goats abominable in sins; but having numbered me with the sheep on the right hand, save me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

items.english_text: The daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river's side; and when she saw the ark in the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it. And when she had opened it, she saw the child weeping in the ark; and the daughter of Pharaoh had compassion on him, and said: "This is one of the Hebrews' children." Then said his sister to Pharaoh's daughter: "Wilt thou that I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?" And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: "Go." And the maid went and called the child's mother. And Pharaoh's daughter said unto her: "Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages." And the woman took the child, and nursed it. And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son; and she called his name Moses, saying: "Because I drew him out of the water."

items.english_text: It came to pass on that day, when Job's sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house, that there came a messenger unto Job, and said: "The oxen were plowing, and the she-asses feeding beside them; and the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away, and have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped and I only am escaped alone to tell thee." While he was yet speaking, there came also another messenger unto Job, and said: "The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and consumed the shepherds likewise; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee." While he was yet speaking, there came also another messenger unto Job, and said: "The Chaldeans made out three bands, and surrounded the camels, and have carried them away, and have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee." While he was yet speaking, there came also another messenger, and said unto Job: "Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house; and behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee." Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and sprinkled dust upon his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped the Lord, and said: "Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; as it pleased the Lord, so is it done: blessed be the name of the Lord unto the ages!" In all these things that befell him, Job sinned not, nor with his lips, nor did he charge God with folly.

items.slavonic_text: НА ПА́ВЕЧЕРНИЦИ ПОЕ́МЪ ТРІПѢ́СНЕЦЪ Творе́нїе Кѵ́ръ А҆ндре́а Кри́тскагѡ. Гла́съ, в҃. Пѣ́нь, в҃. И҆рмо́съ. Непло́днаго оу҆ма̀ моего̀, плодоно́сна Бж҃е покажѝ, дѣ́лателю до́брымъ, и҆ насади́телю бл҃гимъ, мл҃рдїемъ си:. Кончи́нѣ вре́мя, ѡ҆врати́мся про́чее, Хс҃ оу҆чи́тъ: прїи́детъ бо въ мгнове́нїи, прїи́детъ и҆ не оу҆медли́тъ, сꙋди́ти мі́рꙋ всемꙋ̀:. Внеза́пное своего̀ прише́ствїя Хс҃ явля́я, речѐ, Но́ево дре́вле ненаде́ждное тлѣ́нїе, навести́ся хотя́щее землѝ:. Ѡ҆ве́рзеся черто́гъ, оу҆краси́ся сны́мъ Бж҃твенныи бра́къ, Жени́хъ бли́зъ, призыва́яй на́съ. оу҆готови́мся про́чее:. Сі́мсонѡвъ до́мъ, невмѣсти́маго вездѐ, въмѣсти́ тя І҆с҃е Цр҃ю, и҆ жена̀ грѣ́шная мѵ́ромъ тя пома́за:. Бл҃гово́нїа таин̾ственнагѡ и҆спо́лнена жена̀, пе́рвагѡ и҆зба́вльшися злово́нїа Сп҃се, мно́гихъ съгрѣше́нїй, мѵ́ро бо пита́еши жи́зни:. Не́ная пи́ще, а҆́лчꙋщымъ живо́те, са́мъ сы́и, я҆́лъ є҆си Хе҃ съ чл҃ки, проявля́я снисхожде́нїе твоѐ. Неразꙋ́мный Оу҆чени́къ ѿве́ргся тебе Хрⷭ҇те, съко́рище беззако́нныхъ людїѝ подвиза́етъ на тя, на преда́нїе ѡ҆бращься:. Сла́ва: Съ Ѻ҆тце́мъ ти Сн҃ꙋ, и҆ Дх҃ꙋ пра́вомꙋ, є҆ди́номꙋ Е҆стество̀ покланя́юся, и҆ вопѣва́ю ли́цы раздѣля́я, и҆ сꙋщество́мъ съвовокупля́я:. И҆ ны́нѣ: Бг҃ородиченъ. Ро́ждшая тя А҆́гница, Па́стыря и҆ А҆́гньца, при́снѡ

Непло́днаго оу҆ма̀ моего̀, плодоно́сна Бж҃е покажѝ, дѣ́лателю до́брымъ, и҆ насади́телю бл҃гимъ, мл҃рдїемъ си:. Кончи́нѣ вре́мя, ѡ҆врати́мся про́чее, Хс҃ оу҆чи́тъ: прїи́детъ бо въ мгнове́нїи, прїи́детъ и҆ не оу҆медли́тъ, сꙋди́ти мі́рꙋ всемꙋ̀:. Внеза́пное своего̀ прише́ствїя Хс҃ явля́я, речѐ, Но́ево дре́вле ненаде́ждное тлѣ́нїе, навести́ся хотя́щее землѝ:. Ѡ҆ве́рзеся черто́гъ, оу҆краси́ся сны́мъ Бж҃твенныи бра́къ, Жени́хъ бли́зъ, призыва́яй на́съ. оу҆готови́мся про́чее:. Сі́мсонѡвъ до́мъ, невмѣсти́маго вездѐ, въмѣсти́ тя І҆с҃е Цр҃ю, и҆ жена̀ грѣ́шная мѵ́ромъ тя пома́за:. Бл҃гово́нїа таин̾ственнагѡ и҆спо́лнена жена̀, пе́рвагѡ и҆зба́вльшися злово́нїа Сп҃се, мно́гихъ съгрѣше́нїй, мѵ́ро бо пита́еши жи́зни:. Не́ная пи́ще, а҆́лчꙋщымъ живо́те, са́мъ сы́и, я҆́лъ є҆си Хе҃ съ чл҃ки, проявля́я снисхожде́нїе твоѐ. Неразꙋ́мный Оу҆чени́къ ѿве́ргся тебе Хрⷭ҇те, съко́рище беззако́нныхъ людїѝ подвиза́етъ на тя, на преда́нїе ѡ҆бращься:. Сла́ва: Съ Ѻ҆тце́мъ ти Сн҃ꙋ, и҆ Дх҃ꙋ пра́вомꙋ, є҆ди́номꙋ Е҆стество̀ покланя́юся, и҆ вопѣва́ю ли́цы раздѣля́я, и҆ сꙋщество́мъ съвовокупля́я:. И҆ ны́нѣ: Бг҃ородиченъ. Ро́ждшая тя А҆́гница, Па́стыря и҆ А҆́гньца, при́снѡ
items.english_text: Together with the Father I worship Thee, O Son, and the Right Spirit, one Nature, and I sing praise, dividing the Persons and uniting the Essence!

items.slavonic_text: при́снѡ мл҃итъ І҆с҃е Бж҃е, ѡ҆ всѣ́хъ лю́дехъ вѣ́рꙋющихъ в тя:. Сѣда́ленъ. Гла́съ, а҆. Подо́бенъ. Ли́къ А҆́гглскїй: Сѐ лꙋка́вое со́нмище въи́стиннꙋ събра́ся, неи́стовнѡ ꙗ҆́кѡ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нника ѡ҆сꙋди́ти, го́рѣ сѣ́дящагѡ ꙗ҆́кѡ сꙋдїю всѣ́хъ Гдⷭ҇я. Нн҃ѣ събира́ется съ Пїла́томъ И҆́рѡдъ. А҆́нна вкꙋ́пѣ же съ Каїа́фою и҆спитꙋ́ютъ, є҆ди́наго долготерпѣливаго:. Пѣ́нь, и҆́. И҆рмо́съ. Въ Кꙋпи́нѣ Мѡѷсе́и Дѣ́вство твоє̀, на Сїна́йстѣй горѣ̀ проѡбрази́вшаго дре́вле: по́йте вся дѣ́ла Гдⷭ҇а, и҆ превозноси́те є҆го̀ въ вѣ́ки. Не невѣ́дый вре́мя на́шегѡ сконча́нїя, Держа́и вѣ́ки, де́нь ѻ҆́ныи невѣ́дѣти преречѐ. но предѣ́лы всѣ́мъ положѝ къ смиреномꙋ́дрїю:. Дре́вꙋ оу҆подо́бихся, селꙋ̀, и҆ храми́нѣ, въ є҆́же жи́ти дꙋшѐ моя̀. Тѣ́мже стяжѝ къ Бг҃ꙋ гото́во срⷣце, да не что̀ тлѣ́нїемъ пло́ти ѡ҆ста́виши:. Е҆гда̀ ся́деши Сꙋдїя̀, разлꙋча́я ꙗ҆́коже ре́клъ є҆сѝ, Па́стырю ѿ ѻ҆ве́цъ ко́злища Сп҃се, стоя́нїя ѻ҆́нагѡ и҆зба́ви на́съ, нелиши́ же на́съ Бж҃твенныя десни́ца твоея̀:. Ты̀ є҆сѝ Па́сха на́ша, пожре́ныи за брѣ́хъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ А҆́гнецъ и҆ же́ртва, и҆ съгрѣше́нїемъ ѡ҆чище́нїе, и҆ твоя̀ Бж҃твенныя стрⷵти превъзноси́мъ Хрⷭ҇те въ вся вѣ́ки:. Не къ Фарисе́омъ сп҃се, ни къ Сі́мсонꙋ то́кмѡ и҆зво́лилъ є҆сѝ, въ хра́мъ на снѣ́дь внити, оу҆же́ и҆ Мытарѣ̀ вкꙋ́пѣ, и҆ блꙋ́дница твоѐ почерпа́ютъ мл҃рдїе:. ѽ бл҃же́нныхъ рꙋ́къ! ѽ бла́говъ и҆ оу҆́стенъ, цѣломꙋ́дренаѧ блꙋ́дница! и҆́миже возлїя̀ сп҃сꙋ мѵ́ро на но́зѣ твоѝ, ѡ҆тира́ющи и҆́хъ, и҆ ча́стѡ ѡ҆блобыза́ющи:. Възлежа́щꙋ тебѣ̀ Сло́ве, жена̀ приста́вши и҆ оу҆ но́гꙋ рыда́ющи, стекляни́цꙋ сп҃се и҆стощѝ мѵ́ра на главꙋ̀ тебѐ безсме́ртнагѡ мѵ́ра:. Бл҃вимъ Ѻ҆ц҃а и҆ Сн҃а и҆ Ст҃гѡ Дх҃а, Гдⷭ҇а. Съ Ѻ҆ц҃емъ Сн҃а и҆ Ст҃а́гѡ Дх҃а, ст҃ꙋю Тр҃цꙋ въ Бж҃твѣ̀ є҆ди́номъ, сла́вимъ вопїюще: Ст҃ъ, Ст҃ъ, Ст҃ъ є҆сѝ въ вѣ́ки:. И҆ ны́нѣ: Бг҃ородиченъ. Мл҃твами Хрⷭ҇те пречт҃ыя ти Мт҃ре, и҆ твои́хъ А҆́пⷵтолъ, мл҃ти твоя̀ намъ низпосли бога́тнѡ, и҆ ми́ръ тво́й пода́ждь лю́демъ твои́мъ:. Та́же, Хва́лимъ бл҃вимъ покланя́емъся Гдⷭ҇ви: И҆рмо́съ. Въ Кꙋпи́нѣ Мѡѷсе́и дѣ́вское чꙋдо: Пѣ́нь, ѳ҃. И҆рмо́съ. Па́че є҆стества̀ пло́тїю заче́ншꙋю въ оу҆тро́бѣ, ѿ Ѻ҆ц҃а безлѣ́тнѡ просїя́вшаго Сло́ва, є҆ди́нꙋ Бц҃ꙋ велича́емъ вѣ́рнѡ:. Дѣла́нїя вре́мя, сп҃се́нїа намѣ́ренїе, тала́нтъ взе́мши, дре́внїй ѡ҆́бразъ дꙋшѐ моя̀, кꙋпѝ вѣ́чнꙋю жи́знь:. Ꙗ҆́кѡ свѣти́лники свѣ́тлыя оу҆краси́вше дꙋшя̀, Жени́хꙋ приходя́щꙋ, къ нетлѣ́нномꙋ бра́кꙋ пре́жде заключе́нїа две́рїй, съвнидѣ́мъ ко́нь:. Хлѣ́бъ сы́и живо́тныи, снѣда́еши І҆с҃е съ Сі́мсономъ Фарісе́омъ, да блꙋ́дница приѡбрѧ́щетъ некꙋпи́мꙋю бл҃гть твою̀, и҆злїя́нїемъ мѵ́ра:. Показа́ти хотя̀ І҆с҃е, пресꙋще́ственное твоегѡ̀ смире́нїя всѣ́мъ, снѣ́лъ є҆си въ домо̀ Сі́мсоновѣ вече́рявъ, а҆́лчꙋщимъ пи́ще:. Пристꙋ́пль

items.english_text: *Ode 8. Heirmos:* Unto Him Who prefigured thy virginity of old in the Bush unto Moses upon Mount Sinai: sing, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages![^232]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto Him Who prefigured thy virginity of old in the Bush unto Moses upon Mount Sinai: sing, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages![^232]
